paras.en: [[1:15|That day is a day of wrath, a day of tribulation and distress, a day of calamity and misery|Dies iræ dies illa, dies tribulationis et angustiæ, dies calamitatis et miseriæ]]; [[1:15|a day of darkness and obscurity|dies tenebrarum et caliginis]], of which the Psalmist says, [[Ps 96:2|Clouds and darkness are round about him|Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus]]; [[1:15|a day of clouds and whirlwinds|dies nebulæ et turbinis]], according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 49:3|A fire shall burn before him: and a mighty tempest shall be round about him|Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet, et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida]]; [[1:16|A day of the trumpet and alarm|dies tubæ et clangoris]]: for the Apostle says to the Thessalonians, For [[1 Thess 4:15|the Lord himself shall come down from heaven with commandment and with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God|ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce archangeli et in tuba Dei descendet de cœlo]]; and again, [[1 Cor 15:52|In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet|In momento, in ictu oculi, in novissima tuba]] we shall rise again, [[1 Cor 15:52|for the trumpet shall sound|canet enim tuba]]; [[1:16|against the fenced cities|super civitates munitas]], that is, communities fenced about with the goods of this world, [[1:16|and against the high bulwarks|et angulos excelsos]], that is, the higher ones, to whom others flee as to corners [*angulos*, "corners", which the Douay-Rheims renders "bulwarks"].

paras.t: Hæc omnia de die judicii convenientissime intelliguntur : cujus tribulatio tanto major erit super iniquos præ omnibus tribulationibus vitæ præsentis, quanto veritas præcedit figuram et claritas umbram, ita ut sanctus Job oret : Quis mihi tribuat ut in inferno protegas me, et abscondas me, donec pertranseat furor tuus, et constituas mihi tempus in quo recorderis mei? Verumtamen dies illa erit electis jucunda, quemadmodum in Evangelio ait Salvator : His autem fieri incipientibus, levate capita vestra, quia appropinquat redemptio vestra.
paras.en: All these things are most fittingly understood of the day of judgment: whose tribulation upon the wicked will be as much greater than all the tribulations of the present life as truth surpasses the figure and brightness the shadow, so that holy Job prays: [[Job 14:13|Who will grant me this, that thou mayst protect me in hell, and hide me till thy wrath pass, and appoint me a time when thou wilt remember me?|Quis mihi tribuat ut in inferno protegas me, et abscondas me, donec pertranseat furor tuus, et constituas mihi tempus in quo recorderis mei?]] Yet that day will be joyful to the elect, as the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Luke 21:28|But when these things begin to come to pass|His autem fieri incipientibus]], [[Luke 21:28|lift up your heads, because your redemption is at hand|levate capita vestra, quia appropinquat redemptio vestra]].

paras.t: Et tribulabo homines, qui sensualitatem sectati sunt : sicut illi quibus prima ad Corinthios ait Apostolus : Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne carnales estis, et secundum hominem ambulatis? Et ambulabunt ut cæci, id est gratiæ claritate privati, sicque perversi in infernum descendent. Et effundetur sanguis eorum, id est, vita ipsorum damnabitur. Solet enim per sanguinem in Scripturis vita designari, juxta illud Ezechielis : Si non annuntiaveris impio, ut avertatur a via sua mala, sanguinem ejus de manu tua requiram. Et corpora eorum sicut stercora in tartarum diffundentur.
paras.en: [[1:17|And I will distress men|Et tribulabo homines]], who have followed sensuality: like those to whom the Apostle says in the first to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:3|whereas there is among you envying and contention, are you not carnal and walk you not according to man?|Quum sit inter vos zelus et contentio, nonne carnales estis, et secundum hominem ambulatis?]] [[1:17|and they shall walk like blind men|Et ambulabunt ut cæci]], that is, deprived of the brightness of grace, and so, perverse, they will go down into hell. [[1:17|and their blood shall be poured out|Et effundetur sanguis eorum]], that is, their life will be damned. For in the Scriptures life is usually signified by blood, according to that of Ezechiel: If thou declare it not to the wicked, [[Ezech 3:18|that he may be converted from his wicked way|ut avertatur a via sua mala]], [[Ezech 3:18|I will require his blood at thy hand|sanguinem ejus de manu tua requiram]]. [[1:17|and their bodies as dung|Et corpora eorum sicut stercora]] shall be poured out into Tartarus.

paras.t: Sed et argentum eorum et aurum eorum non poterit liberare eos. Per argentum intelligi potest sæcularis vel philosophica scientia; per aurum, sapientia theologicalis. Et certum est, quod in die judicii vanis et tumidis ista non proderunt, sed oberunt magis. Scienti enim bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi. Unde et in Isaia scriptum est : Sapientia et scientia tua decepit te; et ibidem, Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris. Similiter exteriores divitiæ tunc juvare non poterunt, juxta illud in Job : Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet; apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia. In igne enim zeli Domini devorabitur omnis terra, id est, omnis terrenus atque carnalis in fervore divinæ justitiæ tunc peribit, quia consummationem, id est omnimodam et finalem damnationem, cum festinatione faciet cunctis habitantibus terram, quorum conversatio non est in cœlis, sed temporalibus magis quam æternis inhærent. De quibus loquitur Jeremias : Domine, omnes qui te derelinquunt, confundentur; recedentes a te, in terra scribentur.
paras.en: [[1:18|Neither shall their silver and their gold be able to deliver them|Sed et argentum eorum et aurum eorum non poterit liberare eos]]. By *silver* can be understood secular or philosophical knowledge; by *gold*, theological wisdom. And it is certain that on the day of judgment these will not profit the vain and the puffed up, but will rather harm them. [[Jas 4:17|To him therefore who knoweth to do good and doth it not, to him it is sin|Scienti enim bonum et non facienti, peccatum est illi]]. Hence it is written also in Isaias: [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia et scientia tua decepit te]]; and in the same book, [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes|Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris]]. Likewise outward riches will then be of no avail, according to that in Job: [[Job 27:19|The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him|Dives quum dormierit, nihil secum auferet]]; [[Job 27:20|Poverty like water shall take hold on him|apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia]]. [[1:18|all the land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy|In igne enim zeli Domini devorabitur omnis terra]], that is, everyone earthly and carnal will then perish in the heat of the divine justice; [[1:18|for he shall make even a speedy destruction|quia consummationem]], that is, an utter and final damnation, [[1:18|of all them that dwell in the land|cum festinatione faciet cunctis habitantibus terram]], whose conversation is not in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], but who cleave to temporal things more than to eternal. Of whom Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 17:13|O Lord|Domine]], [[Jer 17:13|all that forsake thee shall be confounded: they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth|omnes qui te derelinquunt, confundentur; recedentes a te, in terra scribentur]].

paras.t: Ecce quam fructuosus et pulcher est mysticus hujus capituli intellectus.
paras.en: Behold how fruitful and beautiful is the mystical understanding of this chapter.

paras.t: Postremo, circa illud quod dictum est, Disperierunt omnes involuti argento, ait B. Hieronymus : Neque putandum est, eos solos periisse qui argento tecti sunt; sed juxta hanc definitionem peribit et ille qui de generis nobilitate se jactat, peribit qui inflatur dignitatibus, peribit qui corporis fortitudine gloriatur; peribit qui femineo languore mollitus, comam nutrit, vellit pilos, cutem polit, et ad speculum comitur : quæ propria passio et insania feminarum est.
paras.en: Lastly, concerning what was said, [[1:11|all are cut off that were wrapped up in silver|Disperierunt omnes involuti argento]], blessed Jerome says: Nor is it to be thought that only those have perished who are covered with silver; but by this definition he too shall perish who boasts of the nobility of his birth; he shall perish who is puffed up with dignities; he shall perish who glories in the strength of his body; he shall perish who, softened with womanish languor, grows his hair long, plucks out his hairs, smooths his skin, and adorns himself before the mirror: which is the proper passion and folly of women.

2.title: Explanatio litteralis capituli secundi: Convenite, congregamini, gens non amabilis.
2.title_en: Literal explanation of the second chapter: Assemble yourselves together, be gathered together, O nation not worthy to be loved.

paras.t: Præcedenti capitulo denuntiavit Propheta Judæorum punitionem; nunc, ne eis quod comminatum est, accidat, invitat eos ad pœnitentiam. Convenite spiritualiter, mente concordi et pari proposito, caritatis vinculo adunati, congregamini corporaliter in templo ad implorandum misericordiam Dei, gens non amabilis, id est vos, Judæi, propter peccata vestra odibiles Deo: qui omnia diligit, quoad id quod ab ipso habent et sunt per naturam vel gratiam, sed perversos odit, quantum ad culpam. Unde per Jeremiam ait ad populum istum: Si Moyses et Samuel steterint coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum. Videtur quoque istud potius referendum ad Judæos qui erant post mortem Josiæ regis, quam ad eos qui sub Josia vixerunt, quia hi Domino servierunt, et erant per actus virtutum amabiles.
paras.en: In the preceding chapter the Prophet announced the punishment of the Jews; now, lest what was threatened should befall them, he invites them to penance. [[2:1|Assemble yourselves together|Convenite]] in spirit, with one mind and a like purpose, united by the bond of charity; [[2:1|be gathered together|congregamini]] in body, in the temple, to implore the mercy of God, [[2:1|O nation not worthy to be loved|gens non amabilis]], that is, you Jews, hateful to God for your sins: for he loves all things as regards what they have and are from him by nature or by grace, but hates the perverse as regards their guilt. Hence through Jeremias he says of this people: [[Jer 15:1|If Moses and Samuel shall stand before me, my soul is not towards this people|Si Moyses et Samuel steterint coram me, non est anima mea ad populum istum]]. This also seems rather to refer to the Jews who lived after the death of King Josias than to those who lived under Josias, for these served the Lord and were worthy to be loved through acts of virtue.

paras.t: Itaque, Convenite velociter, priusquam pariat jussio quasi pulverem transeuntem diem, id est, antequam ista commissio mihi facta, qua vobis pœnas futuras prænuntiavi, inducat super vos diem afflictionis præfatæ, tam cito et copiose ut pulvis volans per ventum adducitur: hoc est, antequam Deus, qui jussit mihi hæc prophetare, ad effectum perducat quæ dixi. Quidam asserunt hanc litteram decurtatam, et supplere aliquid oportere; sed hoc non apparet, quum expositio ista, qua nihil subintelligitur, plana sit, et integrum pariat sensum. Antequam veniat super vos ira furoris Domini, antequam veniat super vos ira indignationis ejus, id est, antequam præscriptam dirissimam tribulationem realiter incurratis. Qualiter autem invariabili et supertranquillissimo Deo ira, furor et indignatio adscribantur, videlicet per similitudinem effectus, non per veritatem affectus seu passionis, dictum est sæpe.
paras.en: Therefore, [[2:1|Assemble yourselves together|Convenite]] quickly, [[2:2|Before the decree bring forth the day as dust passing away|priusquam pariat jussio quasi pulverem transeuntem diem]], that is, before this commission given to me, by which I have foretold to you the punishments to come, brings upon you the day of the affliction spoken of, as swiftly and as thickly as dust flying is carried along by the wind: that is, before God, who commanded me to prophesy these things, brings to effect what I have said. Some assert that this text is cut short and that something must be supplied; but this does not appear, since this explanation, in which nothing has to be understood, is plain and yields a complete sense. [[2:2|before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you|Antequam veniat super vos ira furoris Domini]], [[2:2|before the day of the Lord's indignation come upon you|antequam veniat super vos ira indignationis ejus]] [Denis reads *ira indignationis ejus*, "the wrath of his indignation", where the Vulgate has "the day of the Lord's indignation"], that is, before you actually incur the most dire tribulation described above. But how wrath, fury and indignation are ascribed to God, who is unchangeable and tranquil beyond all tranquillity, namely by a likeness of effect, not by the truth of an affection or passion, has often been said.

paras.t: Quærite Dominum, per eleemosynas, orationes, pœnitentiam atque jejunia, omnes mansueti terræ, id est, qui motum iræ et impatientiam refrenatis. Tales enim Deus singularius et promptius exaudire consuevit, juxta illud in Psalmo: Exaltabit mansuetos in salutem; et alibi, Mansuetorum et humilium tibi semper placuit deprecatio. Qui judicium ejus estis operati, id est, recte judicastis, et recte judicata servastis, ac divina præcepta implestis. Quærite justum, id est Deum totius justitiæ fontem. De quo legitur: Quum sis justus, omnia juste disponis; virtus enim tua, justitiæ initium est. Itemque in Psalmo: Justus es, Domine, et rectum judicium tuum. In Job quoque: Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas; opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet.
paras.en: [[2:3|Seek the Lord|Quærite Dominum]] by alms, prayers, penance and fasts, [[2:3|all ye meek of the earth|omnes mansueti terræ]], that is, you who curb the motion of anger and impatience. For God is wont to hear such as these more particularly and more readily, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 149:4|he will exalt the meek unto salvation|Exaltabit mansuetos in salutem]]; and elsewhere: [[Jdt 9:16|the prayer of the humble and the meek hath always pleased thee|Mansuetorum et humilium tibi semper placuit deprecatio]]. [[2:3|you that have wrought his judgment|Qui judicium ejus estis operati]], that is, you who have judged rightly, and kept to what was rightly judged, and fulfilled the divine precepts. [[2:3|seek the just|Quærite justum]], that is, God, the fountain of all justice, of whom we read: [[Wis 12:15|as thou art just, thou orderest all things justly|Quum sis justus, omnia juste disponis]]; [[Wis 12:16|For thy power is the beginning of justice|virtus enim tua, justitiæ initium est]]. And likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 118:137|Thou art just, O Lord: and thy judgment is right.|Justus es, Domine, et rectum judicium tuum]] In Job too: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from the Almighty|Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas]]; [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet]].

paras.t: Quærite mansuetum, id est Deum, qui longanimis est et præstabilis super malitia, ut habetur in Joele. Porro si mansuetudo proprie accipiatur, ut est virtus moralis passionem iræ refrenans, non convenit Deo proprie, sed nec passio iræ, ceteræque virtutes morales circa passiones versantes; sed per similitudinem actionis, quia frequenter vindictam non statim per modum irati infligit, sed per modum mansueti longanimiter differt. Propter quod ait vir sanctus: Quoniam tu, Domine, suavis et mitis.
paras.en: [[2:3|seek the meek|Quærite mansuetum]], that is, God, who is long-suffering and [[Joel 2:13|ready to repent of the evil|præstabilis super malitia]], as we have it in Joel. Now if meekness is taken in the proper sense, as the moral virtue that curbs the passion of anger, it does not properly befit God, any more than the passion of anger does, or the other moral virtues that are concerned with the passions; but it is said of him by a likeness of action, because he often does not inflict vengeance at once, in the manner of one who is angry, but in the manner of one who is meek defers it with long-suffering. For which reason the holy man says: [[Ps 85:5|For thou, O Lord, art sweet and mild|Quoniam tu, Domine, suavis et mitis]].

paras.t: Si quo modo abscondamini in die furoris Domini, id est, aliquo modo evadere valeatis præinducta divinæ æquitatis flagella a Chaldæis infligenda. Aliqui enim justi tempore Babylonicæ captivitatis evaserunt, ut Jeremias, Baruch, Abdemelech Æthiops de quo in Jeremia habetur, et alii quidam. Sed quia frequenter contingit in hac vita cum impiis simul involvi et justos: quod Deus propter eorum peccata purganda, et ampliorem gratiam in præsenti eis præstandam, gloriamque majorem in patria, nonnunquam permittit (variæ enim sunt causæ tribulationum electorum hominum in hac vita); ideo ait Propheta, quasi ut dubitans, Si quo modo.
paras.en: [[2:3|if by any means you may be hid in the day of the Lord's indignation|Si quo modo abscondamini in die furoris Domini]], that is, if by some means you may escape the scourges of the divine equity foretold above, which are to be inflicted by the Chaldeans. For some just men escaped in the time of the Babylonian captivity, such as Jeremias, Baruch, Abdemelech the Ethiopian, of whom we read in Jeremias[[Jer 38:7||]], and certain others. But because it often happens in this life that the just too are caught up together with the wicked (which God sometimes permits in order to purge their sins, and to bestow on them more abundant grace in the present and greater glory in the fatherland; for the causes of the tribulations of the elect in this life are various), the Prophet therefore says, as though doubting, [[2:3|if by any means|Si quo modo]].

paras.t: Denique ostendit Propheta, quasi per locum a majori, quod utique Judæis ista adversa evenient, quia et urbibus Philistinorum, qui pro tempore de quo nunc sermo fortiores erant Judæis, Babylonii prævalebunt. Quia Gaza destructa erit, et Ascalon in desertum, id est, in solitudinem redigetur, urbe et incolis ejus dejectis; Azotum urbem Philistiim, in meridie ejicient, id est, clara luce seu media die Babylonii destruent; et Accaron civitas eradicabitur a Chaldæis. Hæ fuerunt quatuor principales Philistinorum urbes: per quarum demolitionem totius illius provinciæ vastitas denotatur. De qua tamen clarius subditur:
paras.en: Next the Prophet shows, as it were by an argument from the greater [*locus a majori*, a topic of logic: what befalls the stronger will all the more befall the weaker], that these adversities will certainly befall the Jews, since the Babylonians will prevail even over the cities of the Philistines, who at the time now spoken of were stronger than the Jews. [[2:4|For Gaza shall be destroyed|Quia Gaza destructa erit]], [[2:4|and Ascalon shall be a desert|et Ascalon in desertum]], that is, it shall be brought to a wilderness, the city and its inhabitants being cast down; [[2:4|they shall cast out|ejicient]] [[2:4|Azotus|Azotum]], a city of the Philistines, [[2:4|at noonday|in meridie]], that is, the Babylonians will destroy it in broad daylight, or at midday; [[2:4|and Accaron|et Accaron]], the city, [[2:4|shall be rooted up|eradicabitur]] by the Chaldeans. These were the four chief cities of the Philistines, and by their demolition the devastation of that whole province is signified; of which, however, it goes on more clearly:

paras.t: Væ temporalis captivitatis, imo etiam perpetuæ damnationis, imminet vobis, qui habitatis funiculum maris, id est Philistæis, quorum terra super mare Mediterraneum sita asseritur, gens perditorum, id est de numero reproborum. Verbum Domini, id est prophetica denuntiatio divinitus inspirata, venit super vos, Chanaan, id est, populus de semine Cham filii Noe exortus, ut patet in Genesi, terra Philistinorum, id est habitatores terræ istius. Quod autem terra Philistinorum fuerit terra Chanaan, scilicet portio ejus, habetur in libro Josue. Erant autem Philistæi idololatræ pessimi, et filiis Israel vehementer molesti. Et disperdam te, ita ut non sit inhabitator, id est, tam graviter per Chaldæos vastaberis, me volente, quod habitatores terræ tuæ deficient, vel simpliciter omnes, vel pene omnes, ita ut remanentes præ paucitate non reputentur.
paras.en: [[2:5|Woe|Væ]] of temporal captivity, nay, even of perpetual damnation, hangs over you [[2:5|that inhabit the sea coast|qui habitatis funiculum maris]] [*funiculus maris*, literally "the little cord of the sea": the strip of coast, measured out as with a line], that is, over the Philistines, whose land is said to lie on the Mediterranean Sea, [[2:5|O nation of reprobates|gens perditorum]], that is, of the number of the reprobate. [[2:5|the word of the Lord|Verbum Domini]], that is, the prophetic denunciation divinely inspired, comes [[2:5|upon you, O Chanaan|super vos, Chanaan]], that is, a people sprung from the seed of Cham the son of Noe, as is plain in Genesis[[Gen 10:6||]], [[2:5|the land of the Philistines|terra Philistinorum]], that is, the inhabitants of that land. And that the land of the Philistines was the land of Chanaan, namely a portion of it, is found in the book of Josue[[Jos 13:3||]]. Now the Philistines were the worst of idolaters, and grievously troublesome to the children of Israel. [[2:5|and I will destroy thee, so that there shall not be an inhabitant|Et disperdam te, ita ut non sit inhabitator]], that is, thou shalt be laid waste so heavily by the Chaldeans, by my will, that the inhabitants of thy land shall fail, either simply all, or almost all, so that those who remain are of no account for their fewness.

paras.t: Et erit funiculus maris, id est terra Philistinorum, requies pastorum et caulæ pecorum: quia in ea pastores pecora pascent, et in tuguriis ponent. Destructis enim habitaculis, nascuntur gramina animalium pascuis apta.
paras.en: [[2:6|And the sea coast shall be|Et erit funiculus maris]], that is, the land of the Philistines, [[2:6|the resting place of shepherds, and folds for cattle|requies pastorum et caulæ pecorum]]: for in it shepherds shall pasture their flocks and put them in huts. For when the dwellings are destroyed, grasses spring up fit for the pasture of animals.

paras.t: Et erit funiculus ejus, id est, terra ista in eorum usum deveniet, qui remanserint de domo Juda, id est reliquiis Judæorum de Babylonica captivitate redeuntium. Ibi pascentur greges eorum, et ipsi simul vescentur; in domibus Ascalonis ad vesperam requiescent: id est, ubi aliquando fuerunt habitacula urbis hujus, ibi jam sole occidente remanebunt Judæorum pecora et pastores propter abundantiam pascuarum; quia visitabit eos Dominus Deus eorum, scilicet Judæos in Babylone. Hæc visitatio in bono accipitur: utpote pro liberatione a captivitate. Propter quod subditur: et avertet captivitatem eorum, reducendo eos in terram promissionis cum Esdra, ut legitur in libro Esdræ.
paras.en: [[2:7|And it shall be the portion|Et erit funiculus ejus]] [again *funiculus*, the measuring cord, and so the share measured out], that is, that land shall come into the use [[2:7|of him that shall remain of the house of Juda|qui remanserint de domo Juda]], that is, of the remnant of the Jews returning from the Babylonian captivity. [[2:7|there they shall feed|Ibi pascentur]], that is, their flocks shall, and they themselves shall eat together with them; [[2:7|in the houses of Ascalon they shall rest in the evening|in domibus Ascalonis ad vesperam requiescent]]: that is, where the dwellings of that city once stood, there now at sunset the flocks and shepherds of the Jews shall stay, because of the abundance of pasture; [[2:7|because the Lord their God will visit them|quia visitabit eos Dominus Deus eorum]], namely the Jews in Babylon. This visitation is taken in a good sense, as meaning deliverance from captivity. For which reason it is added: [[2:7|and bring back their captivity|et avertet captivitatem eorum]], by leading them back into the land of promise with Esdras, as we read in the book of Esdras[[1 Esd 1:1||]][[1 Esd 2:1||]][[1 Esd 7:1||]].

paras.t: Consequenter vaticinatur Propheta contra Moabitas et Ammonitas. Quemadmodum enim in majoribus Prophetis, Isaia, Jeremia, Ezechiele, consuetudinis est ut post comminationes propheticas ad populum Israel pertinentes, contra gentes ei vicinas prophetetur, eo quod de adversitate Israel vitiose lætatæ sint, vel eorum oppressioni cooperatæ; ita nunc Sophonias procedit.
paras.en: Next the Prophet prophesies against the Moabites and the Ammonites. For just as in the greater Prophets, Isaias, Jeremias and Ezechiel, it is customary that after the prophetic threats concerning the people of Israel there should be prophecy against the nations neighbouring it, because they rejoiced wickedly at Israel's adversity, or had a hand in their oppression, so Sophonias now proceeds.

paras.t: Audivi ego Deus, universa cognoscens: itaque, Audivi, id est, intra me intellectualiter, non de novo, sed ab æterno cognovi, et nunc me id scire per effectum ostendo: propter quod audire me dico, quia per modum aliquid de novo percipientis me habeo. Unde in libro Sapientiæ habetur: Auris zeli audit omnia.
paras.en: [[2:8|I have heard|Audivi]], I, God, who know all things. Thus, [[2:8|I have heard|Audivi]], that is, I have known within myself, intellectually, not newly but from eternity, and now I show by the effect that I know it: for which reason I say that I hear, because I bear myself in the manner of one who perceives something newly. Hence in the book of Wisdom we have: [[Wis 1:10|the ear of jealousy heareth all things|Auris zeli audit omnia]].

paras.t: Opprobrium Moab, id est derisionem Moabitarum et insultationem eorum contra Judæos, et blasphemias filiorum Ammon, quia et Deo et populo ejus verbis perfidiæ derogaverunt, quasi Deus eorum non potuisset eis succurrere; quæ exprobraverunt populo meo Israel, quem elegi et meo cultui specialiter deputavi. Hinc per Isaiam loquitur Deus: Hereditas mea Israel. Et magnificati sunt super terminos eorum, vel de vastitate Judææ magnifice gloriando, vel aliquid de terra illa suo territorio adjungendo, quia ex una parte fuerunt vicini.
paras.en: [[2:8|the reproach of Moab|Opprobrium Moab]], that is, the derision of the Moabites and their insults against the Jews, [[2:8|and the blasphemies of the children of Ammon|et blasphemias filiorum Ammon]], because with faithless words they disparaged both God and his people, as though their God had not been able to help them; [[2:8|with which they reproached my people|quæ exprobraverunt populo meo]] Israel, whom I chose and set apart specially for my worship. Hence God speaks through Isaias: [[Is 19:25|Israel is my inheritance|Hereditas mea Israel]]. [[2:8|and have magnified themselves upon their borders|Et magnificati sunt super terminos eorum]], either by glorying grandly over the devastation of Judea, or by adding some part of that land to their own territory, since on one side they were its neighbours.

paras.t: Propterea vivo ego, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est angelicorum spirituum atque cœlestium agminum. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt: Dominus virtutum. Iste est quasi modus jurandi ipsius Dei, qui jurare non habet nisi per se ipsum. Denique, ipse essentialiter vivens est fons vitæ, et actualissima, voluptuosissima ac superpurissima vita. Deus Israel: quia Moab ut Sodoma erit, id est, urbes ac populus Moab graviter atque totaliter a Chaldæis vastabuntur, et filii Ammon subvertentur a Chaldæis quasi Gomorrha, id est sicut urbs illa a Deo subversa. Et est similitudo non totalis, sed aliqualis: reædificata sunt enim regna Moab et Ammon. Siccitas spinarum erit ibi, videlicet spinæ et vepres, et acervi salis, per quod terræ sterilitas insinuatur, et desertum, id est inhabitabilis solitudo, usque in æternum. Non videtur hoc verum, quia (ut tactum est) provinciæ istæ ad statum pristinum redierunt. Ad quod respondet S. Hieronymus, quod dictio Hebraica loco hoc posita, significat æternitatem et sæculum. Si ergo pro æterno sumatur, sensus est quod regna ista post præscriptam pressuram regnum proprium amiserunt, id est reges de genere suo, et ab alienis regibus tenebantur. Si vero accipiatur pro sæculo, intelligendum est quod dejectio illa pro aliquanto vel longo tempore, vel pro una quadam ætate duraverit. Porro responsio ista magistralior (* alias aptior) est, quam quod aliqui asserunt in Hebræo haberi, Usque in sæculum.
paras.en: [[2:9|Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts|Propterea vivo ego, dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, of the angelic spirits and the heavenly armies; hence the Septuagint translated: the Lord of powers. This is, as it were, the manner of swearing of God himself, who has none to swear by but himself[[Heb 6:13||]]. Indeed he, living by his very essence, is the fountain of life, and is life most actual [that is, wholly in act, with nothing merely potential], most delightful, and pure beyond all purity. [[2:9|the God of Israel|Deus Israel]]: [[2:9|Moab shall be as Sodom|quia Moab ut Sodoma erit]], that is, the cities and people of Moab shall be laid waste heavily and completely by the Chaldeans, [[2:9|and the children of Ammon|et filii Ammon]] shall be overthrown by the Chaldeans [[2:9|as Gomorrha|quasi Gomorrha]], that is, like that city overthrown by God. And the likeness is not total but partial, for the kingdoms of Moab and Ammon were built up again. [[2:9|the dryness of thorns|Siccitas spinarum]] shall be there, namely thorns and briars, [[2:9|and heaps of salt|et acervi salis]], by which the barrenness of the land is suggested, [[2:9|and a desert|et desertum]], that is, an uninhabitable wilderness, [[2:9|even for ever|usque in æternum]]. This does not seem true, since (as was touched on) these provinces returned to their former state[[Jer 48:47||]] [the margin gives Jer. xlviii, 47, which speaks of Moab; for Ammon compare Jer 49:6]. To this St. Jerome answers that the Hebrew word set in this place signifies both eternity and an age. If then it is taken for the eternal, the sense is that after the oppression described these kingdoms lost a kingdom of their own, that is, kings of their own race, and were held by foreign kings. But if it is taken for an age, it is to be understood that that overthrow lasted for some time, or for a long time, or for one particular age. And this answer is more masterly [a variant reading, given in the edition's footnote, has *aptior*, "more apt"] than what some assert, that the Hebrew has: Even for an age.

paras.t: Reliquiæ populi mei, id est Judæi a Babylone reversi, eorumve posteri, diripient eos, id est, sibi eos subjicient; residui gentis meæ Israeliticæ, possidebunt illos, id est, Moabitas ac Ammonitas suæ ditioni substernent. Quod tempore Machabæorum fertur impletum, ut in primo libro Machabæorum aliqualiter innotescit. Verumtamen, ut dicit Hieronymus, Judæi non bene valent ostendere hæc esse impleta post reditum a Babylone ante Christi adventum. Propter quod aliqui Judæorum affirmant hæc in adventu Messiæ, quem inaniter præstolantur, esse adimplenda. Contra quod Hieronymus efficaciter disputat: imo in expositione hujus capituli et alibi, fortiter probat litteralem Judæorum expositionem interdum stare non posse. Nihilominus dicit se quod ab Hebræis accepit ac didicit, litteralem videlicet expositionem, Latinorum auribus tradere.
paras.en: [[2:9|the remnant of my people|Reliquiæ populi mei]], that is, the Jews returned from Babylon, or their descendants, [[2:9|shall make a spoil of them|diripient eos]], that is, shall subject them to themselves; [[2:9|the residue of my nation|residui gentis meæ]], the nation of Israel, [[2:9|shall possess them|possidebunt illos]], that is, shall bring the Moabites and Ammonites under their dominion. This is said to have been fulfilled in the time of the Machabees, as is made known after a fashion in the first book of Machabees[[1 Mach 5:6||]] [the margin gives 1 Mach. v, 6–8, Judas's war against the children of Ammon]. Yet, as Jerome says, the Jews cannot well show that these things were fulfilled after the return from Babylon, before the coming of Christ. For this reason some of the Jews affirm that these things are to be fulfilled at the coming of the Messias, whom they vainly await. Against this Jerome argues effectively; indeed, in his exposition of this chapter and elsewhere, he proves forcefully that the literal exposition of the Jews sometimes cannot stand. Nevertheless he says that he is handing on to the ears of the Latins what he received and learnt from the Hebrews, namely the literal exposition.

paras.t: Hoc eis eveniet pro superbia sua: id est, calamitas et afflictio ista infligetur Moabitis et Ammonitis propter eorum superbiam; quia blasphemaverunt et magnificati sunt super populum Domini exercituum, Judæos spernendo, irridendo ac blasphemando.
paras.en: [[2:10|This shall befall them for their pride|Hoc eis eveniet pro superbia sua]]: that is, this calamity and affliction shall be inflicted on the Moabites and Ammonites because of their pride; [[2:10|because they have blasphemed, and have been magnified against the people of the Lord of hosts|quia blasphemaverunt et magnificati sunt super populum Domini exercituum]], by despising, mocking and blaspheming the Jews.

paras.t: Horribilis Dominus super eos, id est, per Chaldæos terribiliter eos vastabit, et attenuabit omnes deos terræ, id est, deos seu idola Moab et Ammon conteret per Chaldæos. Et adorabunt eum viri de loco suo, id est, qui unius veri Dei notitiam ex suæ omnipotentiæ effectibus acceperunt, omnes insulæ gentium, id est quidam de omnibus insulis, inter quos habitaverunt Judæi, qui quosdam gentilium ad veri Dei cultum converterunt: sicut in libro Esther plenius edocetur, quemadmodum multi in regno Assueri religioni Judæorum se conjunxerunt. Verumtamen ista convenientius pro tempore Christi et evangelicæ prædicationis exponuntur, quando in toto orbe terrarum seminata est fides catholica et idololatria demolita. Liberatio quippe Judæorum a Babylonica captivitate, fuit figura redemptionis generis humani a diabolica captivitate per Christum. Idcirco Prophetæ de tempore uno ad aliud sæpe descendunt, sicut in Isaia et Jeremia evidenter ostenditur.
paras.en: [[2:11|The Lord shall be terrible upon them|Horribilis Dominus super eos]], that is, he will lay them waste terribly through the Chaldeans, [[2:11|and shall consume all the gods of the earth|et attenuabit omnes deos terræ]], that is, he will crush the gods or idols of Moab and Ammon through the Chaldeans. [[2:11|and they shall adore him every man from his own place|Et adorabunt eum viri de loco suo]], that is, those who have received knowledge of the one true God from the effects of his omnipotence, [[2:11|all the islands of the Gentiles|omnes insulæ gentium]], that is, some from all the islands among which the Jews dwelt, who converted certain of the Gentiles to the worship of the true God: as is taught more fully in the book of Esther, how many in the kingdom of Assuerus joined themselves to the religion of the Jews[[Esth 8:17||]]. Yet these words are more fittingly expounded of the time of Christ and of the preaching of the Gospel, when the Catholic faith was sown throughout the whole world and idolatry demolished. For the deliverance of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity was a figure of the redemption of mankind from the captivity of the devil through Christ. Therefore the Prophets often pass from one time to another, as is plainly shown in Isaias and Jeremias.

paras.t: Quæ demum nunc de Moab et Ammon breviter dicta sunt, in Isaia et Jeremia diversis capitulis plenius describuntur; sed propter brevitatem, cui in omnibus studeo, allegationes reliqui.
paras.en: Lastly, what has now been said briefly of Moab and Ammon is described more fully in Isaias and Jeremias, in various chapters[[Is 15:1||]][[Is 16:1||]][[Jer 48:1||]][[Jer 49:1||]] [the margin gives Is. xv, xvi; Jer. xlviii, xlix, etc.]; but for the sake of brevity, which I aim at in everything, I have left out the citations.

paras.t: Deinceps profertur prophetalis comminatio contra Æthiopes atque Assyrios, qui filiis Israel interdum molestias intulerunt, sicut in libris Regum et Paralipomenon elucescit. Sed et vos, Æthiopes, interfecti gladio meo eritis, id est, gladio Chaldæorum, scilicet regis Babylonis et populi ejus, interficiemini. Horum gladium nominat Deus gladium suum, quoniam eo disponente ac adjuvante, occiderunt Æthiopes, ita quod erant divinæ exsecutores justitiæ. Deus enim frequenter ulciscitur peccata unius gentis per aliam.
paras.en: Then comes the prophetic threat against the Ethiopians and the Assyrians, who at times brought troubles upon the children of Israel, as appears in the books of Kings and Paralipomenon[[4 Kings 15:1||]][[2 Par 12:3||]][[2 Par 14:9||]] [the margin gives 2 Par. xii, 3; xiv, 9; 4 Kings xv–xix]. [[2:12|You Ethiopians, also shall be slain with my sword|Sed et vos, Æthiopes, interfecti gladio meo eritis]], that is, you shall be slain by the sword of the Chaldeans, namely of the king of Babylon and his people. God calls their sword his own sword, because it was by his disposing and with his help that they slew the Ethiopians, so that they were executors of the divine justice. For God often avenges the sins of one nation through another.

paras.t: Et extendet exercitus Chaldæorum manum suam super aquilonem, id est adversus regionem Assyriorum, in aquilonari plaga locatam, et perdet Assur, id est, regnum Assyriorum vastabit, et ponet speciosam, id est Niniven urbem pulcherrimam in regno Assyriorum metropolim (nam et Ninive interpretata est speciosa), in solitudinem, et in invium, ita quod per eam non erit consuetus vel publicus transitus, et quasi desertum, habitatoribus ab ea deficientibus.
paras.en: [[2:13|And he will stretch out|Et extendet]], namely the army of the Chaldeans, [[2:13|his hand upon the north|manum suam super aquilonem]], that is, against the region of the Assyrians, which lies in the northern quarter, [[2:13|and will destroy Assyria|et perdet Assur]], that is, will lay waste the kingdom of the Assyrians, [[2:13|and he will make the beautiful city|et ponet speciosam]], that is, Ninive, a most beautiful city, the metropolis of the kingdom of the Assyrians (for Ninive too is interpreted *beautiful*), [[2:13|a wilderness, and as a place not passable|in solitudinem, et in invium]], so that there will be no customary or public passage through it, [[2:13|and as a desert|et quasi desertum]], its inhabitants failing from it.

paras.t: Et accubabunt in medio ejus greges, omnes bestiæ gentium: quoniam vastitate et planitie ejus diu durante, orientur ibidem gramina bestiarum esui apta. Porro distributio illa, Omnes bestiæ gentium, non est stricte accipienda pro singulis generum, sed pro multitudine vel generibus singulorum, ut moris est in Prophetis. Et onocrotalus et ericius in liminibus ejus morabuntur, vel in locis ubi limina stabant, vel in liminum ruinis. Vox cantantis in fenestra. In fenestrarum ruinis aves sedentes, cantabunt, ut fieri solet in ædificiis derelictis. Corvus in superliminari, id est, in superliminaribus corvi quiescent, quia neminem videbunt habitatorem quem metuant. Quoniam attenuabo robur ejus, potentiam ipsius destruendo.
paras.en: [[2:14|And flocks shall lie down in the midst thereof, all the beasts of the nations|Et accubabunt in medio ejus greges, omnes bestiæ gentium]]: because, as its desolation and levelling last a long time, grasses fit for beasts to eat will spring up there. Now that distribution, [[2:14|all the beasts of the nations|Omnes bestiæ gentium]], is not to be taken strictly, for every single one of each kind, but for a multitude, or for some of every kind [in the terms of the schools: not *pro singulis generum*, "for the individuals of the kinds", but *pro generibus singulorum*, "for the kinds of the individuals"], as is the custom in the Prophets. [[2:14|and the bittern and the urchin shall lodge in the threshold thereof|Et onocrotalus et ericius in liminibus ejus morabuntur]], either in the places where the thresholds stood, or in the ruins of the thresholds. [[2:14|the voice of the singing bird in the window|Vox cantantis in fenestra]]: birds sitting in the ruins of the windows will sing, as usually happens in abandoned buildings. [[2:14|the raven on the upper post|Corvus in superliminari]], that is, ravens will rest on the lintels, because they will see no inhabitant to fear. [[2:14|for I will consume her strength|Quoniam attenuabo robur ejus]], by destroying its power.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta divinæ justitiæ se conformans, et zelo justitiæ pereunti civitati insultans, subjungit: Hæc, scilicet Ninive, est civitas gloriosa, habitans in confidentia: quoniam populus in ea habitans, de sua fortitudine et urbis firmitate multum præsumpsit; quæ dicebat in corde suo, Ego sum, et extra me non est alia amplius, id est, in tantum devenit pompæ tumorem, quod alias urbes comparatione sui, nullius reputavit momenti. Sed de isto supra in expositione Nahum prophetæ dictum est plenius. Quomodo facta est in desertum, id est solitudini similis, factaque est cubile bestiæ, id est quasi stabulum quoddam brutorum? Tanquam Propheta admirans insinuet, hoc divina virtute mirabiliter factum. Omnis qui transit, id est, qui transierit, per eam, id est ejus ruinas, sibilabit, elationi ejus insultando, et movebit manum suam, demonstrando ad quantam cladem perducta sit.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, conforming himself to the divine justice and, out of zeal for justice, taunting the perishing city, adds: [[2:15|This|Hæc]], namely Ninive, [[2:15|is the glorious city that dwelt in security|est civitas gloriosa, habitans in confidentia]]: for the people dwelling in it presumed greatly on their own strength and on the firmness of the city; [[2:15|that said in her heart|quæ dicebat in corde suo]]: [[2:15|I am, and there is none beside me|Ego sum, et extra me non est alia amplius]], that is, it came to such a swelling of pomp that in comparison with itself it reckoned other cities of no account. But this was spoken of more fully above, in the exposition of the prophet Nahum. [[2:15|how is she become a desert|Quomodo facta est in desertum]], that is, like a wilderness, and is become [[2:15|a place for beasts to lie down in|cubile bestiæ]], that is, as it were a stall for brute beasts? As though the Prophet, marvelling, would suggest that this was wonderfully done by divine power. [[2:15|every one that passeth|Omnis qui transit]], that is, who shall pass, [[2:15|by her|per eam]], that is, by her ruins, [[2:15|shall hiss|sibilabit]], taunting her pride, [[2:15|and wag his hand|et movebit manum suam]], showing to what great ruin she has been brought.

2.title: Elucidatio tropologica ejusdem capituli secundi.
2.title_en: Tropological explanation [that is, the moral reading] of the same second chapter.

paras.t: Moraliter autem cuilibet congregationi vel familiæ vitiosæ atque malignantium ecclesiæ dicitur : Convenite, congregamini, gens non amabilis, id est, redite ad cor, ad rectæ rationis judicium, ad divinorum et ecclesiasticorum obedientiam præceptorum, ab exterioribus ad interiora, a carnalibus ad spiritualia, a temporalibus atque terrenis ad cœlestia et æterna, postremo a bonis creatis, caducis, vanis, fallacibus, ad Creatorem omnipotentem, verum Deum, summum, immensum, incommutabile bonum. Et qui per contentiones et lites, aversiones et odia estis dispersi et ab invicem separati, congregamini in una individua caritate, ut sit omnium cor unum et anima una in Domino : quemadmodum ad Philippenses monet Apostolus : Implete gaudium meum, ut idem sapiatis, unanimes, id ipsum sentientes. Denique de hac spirituali congregatione scriptum est in Joanne : Jesus moriturus erat pro gente, et non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum.
paras.en: Morally, now, it is said to any congregation or household given to vice, and to the church of the malignant: [[2:1|Assemble yourselves together, be gathered together, O nation not worthy to be loved|Convenite, congregamini, gens non amabilis]], that is, [[Is 46:8|return|redite]] [[Is 46:8|to the heart|ad cor]], to the judgment of right reason, to obedience to the precepts of God and of the Church; from outward things to inward, from carnal things to spiritual, from temporal and earthly things to heavenly and eternal; and lastly from created goods, perishable, vain and deceitful, to the almighty Creator, the true God, the highest, immeasurable and unchangeable good. And you who are dispersed and separated from one another by contentions and quarrels, by aversions and hatreds, be gathered together in one undivided charity, so that all may have [[Acts 4:32|one heart and one soul|cor unum et anima una]] in the Lord; as the Apostle exhorts the Philippians: [[Phil 2:2|Fulfil ye my joy, that you be of one mind|Implete gaudium meum, ut idem sapiatis]], [[Phil 2:2|being of one accord, agreeing in sentiment|unanimes, id ipsum sentientes]]. Lastly, of this spiritual gathering it is written in John: [[John 11:51|Jesus should die for the nation|Jesus moriturus erat pro gente]], and [[John 11:52|not only for the nation, but to gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed|non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum]].

paras.t: Quæritur, qualiter impii sint gens non amabilis, quum eos jubeamus amare. Sed amabiles sunt, quoad id quod a Deo sortiti sunt; odibiles autem, quoad id quod ex voluntate propria habent. Unde in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Duas gentes odivit anima mea.
paras.en: It is asked how the wicked are a [[2:1|nation not worthy to be loved|gens non amabilis]], since we bid men love them. The answer is that they are worthy to be loved as regards what they have received from God, but hateful as regards what they have from their own will. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: There are [[Ecclus 50:27|two nations which my soul abhorreth|Duas gentes odivit anima mea]] [the margin gives Ecclus. i, 27; the words are Ecclus 50:27].

paras.t: Itaque, Convenite, et pœnitentiam ex caritate, non ex servili timore, peragite, priusquam pariat jussio quasi pulverem transeuntem diem, id est, priusquam divina jussio, qua Deus impios perire præcepit, vobis inducat diem mortis imparatæ, itemque damnationis æternæ, quasi pulverem copiosæ; antequam veniat super vos ira furoris Domini, id est irremediabilis illa vindicta, ac insanabilis plaga morsque secunda. Propter quod orat Psalmista : Domine, ne in furore tuo arguas me; et Jeremias, Corripe me, Domine, verumtamen in judicio, et non in furore tuo, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me. Hinc ait Salvator : Attendite, ne superveniat in vos repentina dies illa.
paras.en: Therefore [[2:1|Assemble yourselves together|Convenite]], and do penance out of charity, not out of servile fear, [[2:2|Before the decree bring forth the day as dust passing away|priusquam pariat jussio quasi pulverem transeuntem diem]]: that is, before the divine decree, by which God has commanded the wicked to perish, brings upon you the day of unprepared death, and likewise of eternal damnation, abundant as the dust; [[2:2|before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you|antequam veniat super vos ira furoris Domini]], that is, that irremediable vengeance, the incurable stroke and [[Apoc 20:14|the second death|morsque secunda]]. For this reason the Psalmist prays: [[Ps 6:2|O Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation|Domine, ne in furore tuo arguas me]][[Ps 37:2||]]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 10:24|Correct me, O Lord, but yet with judgment: and not in thy fury, lest thou bring me to nothing.|Corripe me, Domine, verumtamen in judicio, et non in furore tuo, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me]] Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 21:34|take heed|Attendite]], lest [[Luke 21:34|that day come upon you suddenly|superveniat in vos repentina dies illa]].

paras.t: Quærite Dominum. Omnis enim qui quærit, invenit. Quærite itaque Deum, et intra vos quærite eum : hoc est, cor vestrum ad ipsum convertite, ipsum rogate. Non enim longe est ab unoquoque nostrum, quia in ipso vivimus, movemur et sumus. Omnes mansueti. Quum mansueti jam habeant Deum cordis sui per gratiam possessorem atque mansorem, qualiter quærent eum, nisi ut copiosius atque perfectius habeant eum, clarius cognoscendo, ardentius diligendo, inseparabilius cohærendo, et non tantum pro se, sed pro aliis quoque exaudiantur ab ipso? Si quo modo abscondamini in die furoris Domini, puta in die judicii : non quod ambiguum sit, mansuetos Deumque perseveranter quærentes, tunc esse salvandos ; sed ad insinuandum quam difficile sit salvari, quam item horrendum ac rigorosum sit Dei judicium. Juxta quem modum scriptum est : Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt?
paras.en: [[2:3|Seek the Lord|Quærite Dominum]]. For every one [[Luke 11:10|that seeketh findeth|qui quærit, invenit]]. Seek God, then, and seek him within yourselves: that is, turn your heart to him, and ask him. For he is [[Acts 17:27|not far from every one of us|Non enim longe est ab unoquoque nostrum]], since [[Acts 17:28|in him we live and move and are|in ipso vivimus, movemur et sumus]]. [[2:3|all ye meek|Omnes mansueti]]. Since the meek already have God by grace as the possessor and indweller of their heart, how shall they seek him, except to have him more abundantly and more perfectly, knowing him more clearly, loving him more ardently, cleaving to him more inseparably, and to be heard by him not only for themselves but for others too? [[2:3|if by any means you may be hid in the day of the Lord's indignation|Si quo modo abscondamini in die furoris Domini]], for instance in the day of judgment: not that it is doubtful whether the meek, and those who seek God perseveringly, will then be saved; but to suggest how hard it is to be saved, and again how dreadful and rigorous is the judgment of God. In which manner it is written: [[1 Pet 4:18|if the just man shall scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?|Si justus vix salvabitur, impius et peccator ubi parebunt?]]

paras.t: Quia Gaza destructa erit. Gaza interpretatur, fortitudo ejus : quo designantur in sæculari potentia et corporali fortitudine, vel etiam spirituali potestate, aut meritorum suorum copia, inaniter gloriantes. Hi tales destruuntur a Deo, omne spirituale esse gratiæ et gloriæ amittendo, et mortem tartaream incidendo, quemadmodum in Psalmo cantatur : Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum, sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, et prævaluit in vanitate sua. Econtrario timorati, atque veraciter sapientes et justi, jugiter psallunt : Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam, quia, Deus, susceptor meus es ; Deus meus, misericordia ejus præveniet me. Et Ascalon in desertum : id est, vitiis aggravati, et igne malignitatis succensi, qui multas animas scandalizant, a Deo derelinquentur. Ascalon quippe, ponderata vel ignis homicida interpretatur. Azotum in meridie ejicient : id est, libidinosi et obsceni in ignem æternum projicientur ab angelis in die judicii, qui separabunt malos de medio justorum, et mittent eos in caminum ignis : in meridie, id est, dum electi plenam gloriæ suscipient claritatem. Azotus equidem, ignis generationis interpretatur : quo ardor libidinis designatur. Et Accaron eradicabitur : id est, infructuosi, et aliorum subversores, de electorum consortio segregabuntur. Accaron namque, sterilitas vel eradicatio interpretatur. Omnis enim arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur, et in ignem mittetur. Et Christus in Evangelio ait : Væ homini per quem scandalum venit. Quocontra ait vir justus : Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei.
paras.en: [[2:4|For Gaza shall be destroyed|Quia Gaza destructa erit]]. Gaza is interpreted *his strength*: by which are signified those who glory vainly in worldly power and bodily strength, or even in spiritual power, or in the abundance of their own merits. Such as these are destroyed by God, losing all the spiritual being of grace and glory and falling into the death of hell; as is sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 51:9|Behold the man that made not God his helper: But trusted in the abundance of his riches: and prevailed in his vanity|Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum, sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, et prævaluit in vanitate sua]]. The God-fearing, on the contrary, and the truly wise and just, sing continually: [[Ps 58:10|I will keep my strength to thee: for thou art my protector|Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam, quia, Deus, susceptor meus es]]; [[Ps 58:11|My God, his mercy shall prevent me|Deus meus, misericordia ejus præveniet me]] [prevent: that is, go before]. [[2:4|and Ascalon shall be a desert|Et Ascalon in desertum]]: that is, those weighed down with vices and set alight with the fire of malice, who scandalize many souls, will be forsaken by God. For Ascalon is interpreted *weighed down*, or *murderous fire*. [[2:4|they shall cast out Azotus at noonday|Azotum in meridie ejicient]]: that is, the lustful and obscene will be cast into everlasting fire by the angels on the day of judgment, who [[Matt 13:49|shall separate the wicked from among the just|separabunt malos de medio justorum]], and [[Matt 13:50|shall cast them into the furnace of fire|mittent eos in caminum ignis]]. [[2:4|at noonday|in meridie]], that is, when the elect receive the full brightness of glory. Azotus indeed is interpreted *fire of generation*, by which the heat of lust is signified. [[2:4|and Accaron shall be rooted up|Et Accaron eradicabitur]]: that is, the unfruitful, and those who overthrow others, will be cut off from the fellowship of the elect. For Accaron is interpreted *barrenness* or *rooting up*. For every [[Matt 7:19|tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down, and shall be cast into the fire|arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur, et in ignem mittetur]][[Matt 3:10||]]. And Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 18:7|woe to that man by whom the scandal cometh|Væ homini per quem scandalum venit]]. Against which the just man says: [[Ps 51:10|But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God|Ego autem sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei]].

paras.t: Væ vobis qui habitatis funiculum maris, id est, vitiis inquietudinis, turbulentiæ et amaritudinis immoramini. Mare enim (ut patuit) sua fluctuatione, concussione et amaritudine inquietos, turbulentos, amaros significat; et qui vitiis istis non reluctantur, sed immorantur, funiculum habitant maris. Super hos Spiritus Sanctus non requiescit, qui super humiles et quietos requiescere perhibetur. In Ecclesiastico quoque scriptum est : Non est sensus, ubi abundat amaritudo. Et Apostolus : Operam, inquit, detis ut quieti sitis. Præterea, quoniam possessio juxta mare sita, magna esse solet, saltem circa littus, potest per maris funiculum possessio parva significari : et idem damnationis judicium est his qui circa parva et modica inordinate afficiuntur, videlicet contra caritatem divinam et justitiæ ordinem, quod illis qui circa multa et magna vitiosum habent affectum. Non enim res ipsa, sed affectus in culpa est, quum et aliqui multa possideant sine peccato, et alii pauca cum vitio. Verbum Domini, id est divina comminatio, super vos, Chanaan, id est, populæ vitiosæ commotionis, plebs passionata atque instabilis. Chanaan enim commotio dicitur. Terra Philistinorum. Isti enim sunt terra et populus Philistinorum, id est potione cadentes, quoniam de mundi hujus sapore et vanitate atque divitiis tantum accipiunt, quod præ pessima ebrietate cadunt a summis in ima, non quæ Dei sunt et quæ sursum sapientes, sed quæ super terram.
paras.en: [[2:5|Woe to you that inhabit the sea coast|Væ vobis qui habitatis funiculum maris]] [funiculus, literally "a little cord": the measuring line, and so a strip of land measured out with it; the Douay-Rheims has "sea coast"], that is, you who linger in the vices of restlessness, turbulence and bitterness. For the sea (as has been shown) by its tossing, its shaking and its bitterness signifies the restless, the turbulent and the bitter; and those who do not struggle against these vices, but linger in them, dwell in the cord of the sea. Upon these the Holy Ghost does not rest, who is said to rest upon the humble and quiet[[Is 66:2||]] [the margin gives Is. lxvi, 1, 2: Denis follows the older Latin reading of Is 66:2, "upon whom shall my spirit rest, but upon the humble and quiet?"; the Vulgate has "to him that is poor and little"]. In Ecclesiasticus too it is written: [[Ecclus 21:15|there is no understanding where there is bitterness|Non est sensus, ubi abundat amaritudo]]. And the Apostle: [[1 Thess 4:11|that you use your endeavour|Operam]], he says, [[1 Thess 4:11|to be quiet|detis ut quieti sitis]]. Moreover, since a property lying by the sea is usually large, at least along the shore, a small property can be signified by the cord of the sea: and the same judgment of damnation falls on those who are inordinately attached to small and slight things (that is, against the love of God and the order of justice) as on those who have a vicious attachment to many and great things. For it is not the thing itself but the attachment that is at fault, since some possess much without sin, and others little with vice. [[2:5|the word of the Lord|Verbum Domini]], that is, the divine threat, [[2:5|upon you, O Chanaan|super vos, Chanaan]], that is, people of vicious commotion, a multitude swayed by passion and unstable. For Chanaan means *commotion*. [[2:5|the land of the Philistines|Terra Philistinorum]]. For these are the land and people of the Philistines, that is, *falling by drink*, since they take so much of the savour, vanity and riches of this world that from the worst drunkenness they fall from the heights to the depths, not minding the things of God and [[Col 3:2|the things that are above|quæ sursum]], but [[Col 3:2|the things that are upon the earth|quæ super terram]].

paras.t: Et erit funiculus maris, id est vitia jam præfata, requies pastorum, id est materia gaudii electorum, se ipsos et sibi commissos spiritualibus animæ alimentis pascentium. Lætabitur enim justus quum viderit vindictam. Et caulæ pecorum, id est repausatoria subditorum bonorum : qui in consideratione vanitatis et ultionis pravorum, quasi repausant, de sibi concessa clementia in Domino gloriantur, cautiusque conversari conantur, et in contemplatione æquitatis divinæ quasi obdormiunt et repausant.
paras.en: [[2:6|And the sea coast shall be|Et erit funiculus maris]], that is, the vices already spoken of, [[2:6|the resting place of shepherds|requies pastorum]], that is, matter of joy for the elect, who feed themselves and those committed to them with the spiritual food of the soul. For the [[Ps 57:11|just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur enim justus quum viderit vindictam]]. [[2:6|and folds for cattle|Et caulæ pecorum]], that is, resting places of good subjects: who in considering the vanity and the punishment of the wicked as it were take their rest, glory in the Lord for the mercy granted to themselves, and strive to live more warily; and in contemplating the justice of God they as it were fall asleep and rest.

paras.t: Et erit funiculus ejus his qui remanserint de domo Juda : id est, peccata eorumque vitia qui terrenis insudant, Sanctorum et electorum ditioni subdentur, qui judicabunt nationes dominabunturque populis. Ibi pascentur in domibus Ascalonis : id est, electi impios possidebunt, et in eorum, si quando emendaverint vitam, conversione spiritualiter epulabuntur. Nihilo minus in vita futura punitio impiorum cedit electis in gloriam et pascua vitæ. Quia visitabit eos, scilicet electos, Dominus Deus eorum, per ampliorem gratiæ consolationem et infusionem, ut valeant convertere alios, vel de eorum punitione juste lætari sine offensa, imo et cum complacentia Dei, cujus se voluntati conformant ; et avertet captivitatem eorum, liberando electos de potestate diaboli, servitute peccati, insaniis mundi : aliter digni non essent alios edocere.
paras.en: [[2:7|And it shall be the portion of him that shall remain of the house of Juda|Et erit funiculus ejus his qui remanserint de domo Juda]]: that is, the sins and vices of those who toil over earthly things will be made subject to the dominion of the Saints and the elect, who [[Wis 3:8|shall judge nations, and rule over people|judicabunt nationes dominabunturque populis]]. [[2:7|there they shall feed: in the houses of Ascalon|Ibi pascentur in domibus Ascalonis]]: that is, the elect will possess the wicked, and will feast spiritually on their conversion, if ever they amend their life. Nonetheless, in the life to come the punishment of the wicked turns to the glory of the elect and to the pastures of life. [[2:7|because|Quia]] [[2:7|the Lord their God|Dominus Deus eorum]] [[2:7|will visit them|visitabit eos]], namely the elect, by a fuller consolation and infusion of grace, so that they may be able to convert others, or to rejoice justly at their punishment without offence, nay, even with the good pleasure of God, to whose will they conform themselves; [[2:7|and bring back their captivity|et avertet captivitatem eorum]], by freeing the elect from the power of the devil, the servitude of sin and the follies of the world: otherwise they would not be worthy to teach others.

paras.t: Audivi opprobrium Moab et blasphemias filiorum Ammon, quæ exprobraverunt populo meo. Moab interpretatur, ex patre : per quod hoc loco reprobi et superbi designantur, quibus loquitur Christus, Vos ex patre diabolo estis : qui sunt quasi servi diaboli, qui est rex super omnes filios superbiæ. Ammon interpretatur, filius patris mei : quo falsi fratres atque hæretici exprimuntur, de quibus in Canticis ait Sponsa : Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me. Hi itaque contumeliam faciunt Dei electis, quemadmodum Christus protestatur : Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur. Horum injuriam reputat Deus sibi illatam, sicut ad Paulum effatur, Quid me persequeris? eamque juste ulciscitur, eo quod super terminos electorum suorum magnificati sint, electorum Ecclesiam opprimendo, spoliando, et persequendo.
paras.en: [[2:8|I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the blasphemies of the children of Ammon, with which they reproached my people|Audivi opprobrium Moab et blasphemias filiorum Ammon, quæ exprobraverunt populo meo]]. Moab is interpreted *from the father*: by which in this place the reprobate and the proud are signified, to whom Christ says: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]; who are as it were slaves of the devil, who [[Job 41:25|is king over all the children of pride|rex super omnes filios superbiæ]]. Ammon is interpreted *son of my father*: by which false brethren and heretics are expressed, of whom the Bride says in the Canticle: [[Cant 1:5|the sons of my mother have fought against me|Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me]]. These, then, do insult to God's elect, as Christ declares: [[John 15:20|If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you|Si me persecuti sunt, et vos persequentur]]. God counts the injury they do as done to himself, as he says to Paul: [[Acts 9:4|why persecutest thou me?|Quid me persequeris?]] And he justly avenges it, because they [[2:8|have magnified themselves upon|magnificati sint]] the borders of his elect, oppressing, despoiling and persecuting the Church of the elect.

paras.t: Ideo subditur, quod erunt quasi Sodoma et Gomorrha, quoniam igne et sulfure infernali cruciabuntur ; et siccitas spinarum inerit eis, quia vermis eorum non morietur ; eruntque acervi salis steriles et perditi in æternum, eo quod nunquam pœnitebunt, nec redimentur. Reliquiæ populi mei diripient illos. Jam etenim tactum est, quemadmodum Sancti judicabunt nationes, et dominabuntur populis, et qui nunc a reprobis opprimuntur injuste, in die judicii reprobos opprimient, juste judicando eos cum Salvatore.
paras.en: Therefore it is added that they [[2:9|shall be as Sodom|erunt quasi Sodoma]] and [[2:9|Gomorrha|Gomorrha]], since they will be tormented with the fire and brimstone of hell; and [[2:9|the dryness of thorns|siccitas spinarum]] will be in them, because [[Is 66:24|their worm shall not die|vermis eorum non morietur]]; and they will be [[2:9|heaps of salt|acervi salis]], barren and lost for ever, since they will never repent, nor be redeemed. [[2:9|the remnant of my people shall make a spoil of them|Reliquiæ populi mei diripient illos]]. For it has already been touched on how the Saints [[Wis 3:8|shall judge nations, and rule over people|judicabunt nationes, et dominabuntur populis]], and those who are now unjustly oppressed by the reprobate will on the day of judgment overwhelm the reprobate, justly judging them with the Saviour.

paras.t: Deinde Dominus comminatur. Sed et vos, Æthiopes, interfecti gladio meo eritis. Æthiopes sunt vitiis denigrati in anima : qui gladio Dei, id est sententia oris Christi spiritualiter interficientur, dum æternaliter damnabuntur. De quo gladio scriptum est in Apocalypsi : De ore ejus gladius ex utraque parte acutus exibat.
paras.en: Then the Lord threatens: [[2:12|You Ethiopians, also shall be slain with my sword.|Sed et vos, Æthiopes, interfecti gladio meo eritis]] The Ethiopians are those blackened in soul by vices, who will be slain spiritually by the sword of God, that is, by the sentence of Christ's mouth, when they are eternally damned. Of this sword it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:16|from his mouth came out a sharp two-edged sword|De ore ejus gladius ex utraque parte acutus exibat]][[Apoc 19:15||]].

paras.t: Et extendet manum suam super aquilonem, id est contra eos qui in frigore permanent vitiorum, in quibus caritas Dei refriguit, suntque peccatis quodammodo congelati per duritiam cordis, quoad ea quæ Dei sunt et suæ salutis. Et perdet Assur, id est dirigentes ad mala, qui cæci sunt mente et duces cæcorum. Assur enim dirigens interpretatur, secundum quosdam ; vel secundum Hieronymum, coarguens et convincens, sicque per Assur intelliguntur accusatores fratrum suorum et observatores : quos Dominus perdet, juxta illud Proverbiorum, Qui investigator malorum est, opprimetur ab eis. Et ponet speciosam in solitudinem : id est, omnem congregationem carnalium, quæ se foris perornat, et mundi hujus honore, gloria atque divitiis decoratur, Deus omni suo vano privabit decore, atque ad summam deformitatem pertrahet eam, ut sit invia et deserta, sicut de impio scriptum est : Quæres locum ejus, et non invenies. Denique Ecclesia olim virtutibus pulchra, donis et gratiis Spiritus Sancti polita, circa Antichristi adventum et ipso regnante, quasi in solitudinem redigetur, et pristino suo ornatu privabitur, quando pene omnes fallentur. Tunc enim juxta Apostolum, instabunt tempora periculosa, et erunt homines se ipsos amantes ; eritque discessio ab utroque imperio, spirituali ac temporali.
paras.en: [[2:13|And he will stretch out his hand upon the north|Et extendet manum suam super aquilonem]], that is, against those who remain in the cold of vices, in whom the charity of God has grown cold[[Matt 24:12||]], and who are in a manner frozen by sins through hardness of heart, as regards the things of God and of their own salvation. [[2:13|and will destroy Assyria|Et perdet Assur]], that is, those who direct men to evil, who [[Matt 15:14|are blind|cæci sunt]] in mind [[Matt 15:14|and leaders of the blind|et duces cæcorum]]. For Assur is interpreted *directing*, according to some; or, according to Jerome, *reproving and convicting*: and so by Assur are understood those who accuse and spy on their brethren, whom the Lord will destroy, according to that word of Proverbs: [[Prov 11:27|he that seeketh after evil things, shall be oppressed by them|Qui investigator malorum est, opprimetur ab eis]]. [[2:13|and he will make the beautiful city a wilderness|Et ponet speciosam in solitudinem]]: that is, every gathering of carnal men which adorns itself outwardly and is decked with the honour, glory and riches of this world, God will strip of all its vain beauty, and drag down to utter deformity, so that it may be pathless and deserted; as it is written of the wicked man: [[Ps 36:10|thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it|Quæres locum ejus, et non invenies]]. Lastly, the Church, once fair with virtues and adorned with the gifts and graces of the Holy Ghost, about the coming of Antichrist and during his reign will be reduced as it were to a wilderness and stripped of her former adornment, when nearly all will be deceived. For then, according to the Apostle, [[2 Tim 3:1|shall come dangerous times|instabunt tempora periculosa]], and men [[2 Tim 3:2|shall be lovers of themselves|erunt homines se ipsos amantes]]; and there will be a falling away from both empires, the spiritual and the temporal.

paras.t: Et accubabunt in medio ejus greges, omnes bestiæ gentium, id est, motus sensualitatis, passiones, et concupiscentiæ in corde ipsius per consensum manebunt. Onocrotalus et ericius, id est vitia per bruta hæc significata. Per ericium, qui est animal spinosum ac pungitivum, impatientia denotatur; per onocrotalum, fœtor impuritatis carnalis. Hæc in liminibus ejus morabuntur, id est inferioribus animæ viribus et sensualitate. Vox cantantis in fenestra, id est insultatio dæmonis de perditione hominum gloriantis. Corvus in superliminari, id est, in superiori animi portione erit sordidatio vitiorum, et dilatio omnis boni.
paras.en: [[2:14|And flocks shall lie down in the midst thereof, all the beasts of the nations|Et accubabunt in medio ejus greges, omnes bestiæ gentium]], that is, the motions of sensuality, the passions and the concupiscences will abide in its heart by consent. [[2:14|the bittern and the urchin|Onocrotalus et ericius]] [onocrotalus is properly the pelican, ericius the hedgehog], that is, the vices signified by these brute beasts. By the urchin, which is a spiny and pricking animal, impatience is denoted; by the bittern, the stench of carnal impurity. These [[2:14|shall lodge in the threshold thereof|in liminibus ejus morabuntur]], that is, in the lower powers of the soul and in sensuality. [[2:14|the voice of the singing bird in the window|Vox cantantis in fenestra]], that is, the mockery of the devil glorying over the perdition of men. [[2:14|the raven on the upper post|Corvus in superliminari]], that is, in the higher part of the mind there will be the defilement of vices and the putting off of all good [the raven's cry was heard as cras, cras, "tomorrow, tomorrow": hence delay].

paras.t: Hæc mundanorum hominum collectio est civitas gloriosa in sæculo isto, deliciis, divitiis, atque honoribus vitæ præsentis intenta : quam et homines sæculares arbitrantur beatam, quum prorsus miserrima sit; habitans in confidentia, quia de se ipsa præsumpsit, et posuit carnem brachium suum, propriam fragilitatem non pensans; quæ dicebat, Ego sum, etc., id est, aliis cunctis se prætulit, ut moris est superborum. Quomodo facta est in desertum? id est, quomodo repente dejecta, et facta est cubile bestiæ, id est dæmonum domus? de quibus dicitur : Ne tradas bestiis animam confitentem tibi. Hinc in Psalmo cantatur : Dejecisti eos, dum allevarentur ; quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? subito defecerunt, perierunt propter iniquitatem suam. Et in Job : Vidi iniquos Domino flante perisse. Omnis qui transit per eam, id est, mente lustraverit qualitatem ejus, atque eventum ipsius perpenderit, sibilabit, et movebit manum suam : secundum sensum in fine præcedentis articuli positum.
paras.en: [[2:15|This|Hæc]] gathering of worldly men [[2:15|is the glorious city|est civitas gloriosa]] in this world, bent on the delights, riches and honours of the present life, which worldly men even think blessed, though it is utterly wretched; [[2:15|that dwelt in security|habitans in confidentia]], because she presumed of herself, and made [[Jer 17:5|flesh his arm|carnem brachium suum]], not weighing her own frailty; [[2:15|that said|quæ dicebat]], [[2:15|I am|Ego sum]], etc., that is, she set herself above all others, as is the way of the proud. [[2:15|how is she become a desert|Quomodo facta est in desertum]]? that is, how has she been suddenly cast down and become [[2:15|a place for beasts to lie down in|cubile bestiæ]], that is, a house of demons? Of whom it is said: [[Ps 73:19|Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee|Ne tradas bestiis animam confitentem tibi]]. Hence it is sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 72:18|when they were lifted up thou hast cast them down|Dejecisti eos, dum allevarentur]]; [[Ps 72:19|How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: they have perished by reason of their iniquity|quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? subito defecerunt, perierunt propter iniquitatem suam]]. And in Job: [[Job 4:8|I have seen those who work iniquity|Vidi iniquos]] [[Job 4:9|perishing by the blast of God|Domino flante perisse]]. [[2:15|every one that passeth by her|Omnis qui transit per eam]], that is, whoever surveys her character in his mind and weighs her end, [[2:15|shall hiss, and wag his hand|sibilabit, et movebit manum suam]]: according to the sense set out at the end of the preceding article.

3.title: Provocatrix et redempta civitas, columba.
3.title_en: The provoking and redeemed city, the dove.

paras.t: Væ provocatrix et redempta civitas, columba. Capitulum præsens intricatum est satis, ideoque a diversis multiformiter explanatur, quemadmodum Domino concedente breviter tangam, et quid rationabilius magisque catholice dici videatur, aperiam. Denique aliqui asserunt, in isto capitulo consolationem Judæorum describi. Sed in exordio hujus capituli, increpatio magis quam consolatio ponitur; in prosecutione vero, præsertim circa finem capituli, consolatio magna promittitur. Præterea, sic exponendum est præsens capitulum, ut ad aliorum intentionem faciliter valeat applicari.
paras.en: [[3:1|Woe to the provoking and redeemed city, the dove|Væ provocatrix et redempta civitas, columba]]. The present chapter is intricate enough, and so it is explained in many ways by different writers, as I shall briefly touch upon, the Lord granting, and I shall show what seems the more reasonable and the more catholic thing to say. Now some assert that in this chapter the consolation of the Jews is described. But at the beginning of this chapter rebuke rather than consolation is set down; in its course, however, and especially towards the end of the chapter, great consolation is promised. Moreover, the present chapter is to be expounded in such a way that it can easily be fitted to the meaning the other expositors intend.

paras.t: Væ magnæ afflictionis imminet tibi, o provocatrix et redempta civitas, id est, o Jerusalem, quæ Deum tuis criminibus ad rigorem justitiæ provocasti. Non quod ejus tranquillitas conturbetur, sed quia ad instar animi concitati subito magnam ultionem inducit. Et quoniam Deus a tempore Judicum, civitatem istam et populum Judæorum sæpe de hostibus liberavit, vocatur redempta. Nuncupatur quoque columba, propter innocentes et simplices qui frequenter habitaverunt in ea, vel quia naturæ humanæ innata videtur quædam simplicitas.
paras.en: The woe of great affliction hangs over thee, O [[3:1|provoking and redeemed city|provocatrix et redempta civitas]], that is, O Jerusalem, who by thy crimes hast provoked God to the rigour of justice: not that His tranquillity is disturbed, but because, like a mind roused to anger, He suddenly brings on a great vengeance. And since from the time of the Judges God often delivered this city and the people of the Jews from their enemies, it is called [[3:1|redeemed|redempta]]. It is also named [[3:1|the dove|columba]], because of the innocent and simple who often dwelt in it, or because a certain simplicity seems to be inborn in human nature.

paras.t: Non audivit vocem, id est, divina eloquia non custodivit, nec Prophetarum sermonibus acquievit; et non suscepit disciplinam, id est, divinam correctionem seu instructionem patienter non tulit, neque a vitiis desiit, juxta illud Jeremiæ : Renuerunt accipere disciplinam. In Domino non est confisa : quia non habuit spem formatam, et creaturæ potius quam Creatori fuit innitens; ad Deum suum non appropinquavit per spiritualem accessum, videlicet credendo, sperando, amando, aliarumque virtutum operibus ex caritate insistendo, præsertim latriæ ac pœnitentiæ actibus. Non enim corporaliter atque localiter, sed spiritualiter et interne incircumscriptibili Deo approximamus. Ideo in Isaia loquitur Deus : Cor ejus longe est a me.
paras.en: [[3:2|She hath not hearkened to the voice|Non audivit vocem]], that is, she has not kept the divine utterances, nor given heed to the words of the Prophets; [[3:2|neither hath she received discipline|et non suscepit disciplinam]], that is, she has not patiently borne the divine correction or instruction, nor left off her vices, according to that of Jeremias: [[Jer 5:3|they have refused to receive correction|Renuerunt accipere disciplinam]]. [[3:2|She hath not trusted in the Lord|In Domino non est confisa]]: because she had not formed hope [that is, hope given its form by charity, a living hope], and was leaning on the creature rather than on the Creator; [[3:2|she drew not near to her God|ad Deum suum non appropinquavit]] by a spiritual approach, namely by believing, hoping, loving, and applying herself out of charity to the works of the other virtues, especially to acts of latria [that is, the worship due to God alone] and of penance. For it is not bodily and locally, but spiritually and inwardly, that we draw near to God, who cannot be bounded by any place. Hence God says in Isaias: [[Is 29:13|their heart is far from me|Cor ejus longe est a me]].

paras.t: Principes ejus in medio ejus quasi leones rugientes, id est protervi et immisericordes, pauperum oppressores, judices ejus lupi vespertini, id est similes lupis vespertinis multum voracibus, non relinquebant in mane, id est, subditorum substantiam immoderatissime devoraverunt, imo et innocentes occiderunt. Hinc ab Isaia inducitur : Principes tui infideles. Per eumdem quoque Prophetam loquitur Dominus : Rapina pauperis in domo vestra est. Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis?
paras.en: [[3:3|Her princes are in the midst of her as roaring lions|Principes ejus in medio ejus quasi leones rugientes]], that is, insolent and merciless, oppressors of the poor; [[3:3|her judges are evening wolves|judices ejus lupi vespertini]], that is, like evening wolves, which are very voracious; [[3:3|they left nothing for the morning|non relinquebant in mane]], that is, they devoured the substance of their subjects beyond all measure, and even slew the innocent. Hence Isaias brings in: [[Is 1:23|Thy princes are faithless|Principes tui infideles]]. Through the same Prophet the Lord says also: [[Is 3:14|the spoil of the poor is in your house|Rapina pauperis in domo vestra est]]. [[Is 3:15|Why do you consume my people, and grind the faces of the poor?|Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis?]]

paras.t: Prophetæ ejus vesani, viri infideles: non enim veri, sed pseudo vates fuerunt, de quibus per Jeremiam Dominus protestatur : Ego non misi eos; visionem mendacem et seductionem cordis sui prophetant vobis. Sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum, id est, jus divinum profanarunt : non quod ipsa divinæ legis justitia in se ipsa sordidetur, sed quod ei injustitia misceatur, vel per impietatem penitus inhonoretur ac relinquatur.
