Sic enim per Ezechielem Dominus ubertim affirmat nomen suum sanctum a Judæis inter gentes pollutum. Injuste egerunt contra legem per Moysen datam, peccando in Deum et proximos, insuper et in se ipsos. De quibus in Jeremia habetur : Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus ?
paras.en: [[3:4|Her prophets are senseless, men without faith|Prophetæ ejus vesani, viri infideles]]: for they were not true prophets but false ones, of whom the Lord protests through Jeremias: [[Jer 14:14|I sent them not|Ego non misi eos]]; [[Jer 14:14|they prophesy unto you a lying vision|visionem mendacem]], and [[Jer 14:14|the seduction of their own heart|seductionem cordis sui prophetant vobis]]. [[3:4|her priests have polluted the sanctuary|Sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum]], that is, they have profaned the divine law [*sanctum* is "the holy thing", which the Douay-Rheims renders "the sanctuary"]: not that the justice of the divine law is itself defiled in itself, but that injustice is mixed with it, or that through impiety it is utterly dishonoured and abandoned. For so the Lord affirms abundantly through Ezechiel that His holy name was polluted by the Jews among the nations[[Ezech 36:20||]][[Ezech 36:22||]][[Ezech 43:8||]]. [[3:4|they have acted unjustly against the law|Injuste egerunt contra legem]] given through Moses, sinning against God and their neighbours, and against themselves besides. Of these it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 2:8|The priests did not say: Where is the Lord?|Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus ?]]

paras.t: Dominus justus in medio ejus. Deus enim ubique est, qui ait per Jeremiam : Cœlum et terram ego impleo. Sed quum, Salomone testante, longe sit Dominus ab impiis, quomodo nunc in medio horum tam pessimorum esse narratur? Et respondendum, quod longe est Dominus ab iniquis, quantum ad præsentiam caritatis et gratiæ. Nihilo minus per essentiam suam ubique est: et quantum ad hoc, divinus Dionysius ait, quod Deus est omnibus æque propinquus. Non faciet iniquitatem. Quum ipse sit prima mensura, et regula universæ justitiæ, ideo eo ipso quo ipse aliquid facit, justum est : nec enim potest peccare, quia essentialiter sanctus est. Idcirco unicuique quod meretur, retribuet. Hinc cantamus in Psalmo : Quoniam rectus Dominus Deus noster, et non est iniquitas in eo. Mane, mane, id est celeriter utique. Repetitio enim, certitudinis indicium est, et confirmatio dicti. Judicium suum dabit, id est, justitiæ suæ effectum ostendet contra præfatos iniquos, in luce sapientiæ suæ, id est secundum suæ veritatis censuram ; vel, In luce, id est aperte, ita quod omnibus innotescet ; et non abscondetur. Nescivit autem iniquus confusionem : id est, causam suæ confusionis et vastitatis perversus Judæorum populus non advertit, videlicet propria crimina ; nec consideravit propter quem finem castigarentur a Deo, videlicet ut pœnitentiam agerent. Vel, Nescivit confusionem, id est, salutarem erubescentiam non admisit, de suis iniquitatibus verecundando, juxta illud in Jeremia : Confusione non sunt confusi, et erubescere noluerunt.
paras.en: [[3:5|The just Lord is in the midst thereof|Dominus justus in medio ejus]]. For God is everywhere, who says through Jeremias: [[Jer 23:24|I fill heaven and earth|Cœlum et terram ego impleo]]. But since, as Solomon testifies, [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|longe sit Dominus ab impiis]], how is He now said to be in the midst of men so very wicked? The answer is that the Lord is far from the wicked as regards the presence of charity and grace; but nonetheless He is everywhere by His essence, and as to this the divine Dionysius [that is, Dionysius the Areopagite] says that God is equally near to all. [[3:5|he will not do iniquity|Non faciet iniquitatem]]: since He Himself is the first measure and the rule of all justice, whatever He does is just by the very fact that He does it; for He cannot sin, since He is holy by His essence. Therefore He will render to each what he deserves. Hence we sing in the Psalm: [[Ps 91:16|the Lord our God is righteous, and there is no iniquity in him|Quoniam rectus Dominus Deus noster, et non est iniquitas in eo]]. [[3:5|in the morning, in the morning|Mane, mane]], that is, swiftly indeed: for repetition is a sign of certainty and a confirmation of what is said. [[3:5|he will bring his judgment|Judicium suum dabit]], that is, He will show the effect of His justice against the wicked spoken of above, [[3:5|to light|in luce]], namely the light of His wisdom, that is, according to the verdict of His truth; or, [[3:5|to light|In luce]], that is, openly, so that it will be known to all; [[3:5|and it shall not be hid|et non abscondetur]]. [[3:5|but the wicked man hath not known shame|Nescivit autem iniquus confusionem]]: that is, the perverse people of the Jews did not take notice of the cause of their confusion and devastation, namely their own crimes; nor did they consider for what end they were chastised by God, namely that they might do penance. Or, [[3:5|hath not known shame|Nescivit confusionem]], that is, they did not admit a wholesome blush by being ashamed of their iniquities, according to that in Jeremias: [[Jer 6:15|they were not confounded with confusion|Confusione non sunt confusi]], and they would not blush [Denis reads *noluerunt*, "they would not", where the Vulgate has *nescierunt*, "they knew not how"].

paras.t: Disperdidi gentes, id est, Judæos per adversarios eorum frequenter vastavi. Judæi autem in veteri Testamento sæpe gentes vocantur, juxta illud Judicum : Irritum fecit gens ista pactum meum. Et Moyses loquitur Deo : Respice populum tuum gentem hanc. Et dissipati sunt anguli earum, id est urbes præcipuæ, vel principes populi hujus, in quorum protectione alii confidebant, et in eis quasi in angulis latere optabant. Desertas feci vias eorum, id est ejus gentis jam dictæ, eo quod non sit qui transeat per eas. Viæ enim, viatoribus deficientibus, terrisque vastatis, consueverunt deficere. Desolatæ sunt civitates eorum, videlicet Judæorum, non remanente in eis viro neque ullo habitatore Judæo.
paras.en: [[3:6|I have destroyed the nations|Disperdidi gentes]], that is, I have often laid the Jews waste by means of their enemies. For in the Old Testament the Jews are often called nations [*gentes*, the word also used for the Gentiles], according to that of Judges: [[Judg 2:20|this nation hath made void my covenant|Irritum fecit gens ista pactum meum]]. And Moses says to God: [[Ex 33:13|look upon thy people this nation|Respice populum tuum gentem hanc]]. [[3:6|and their towers are beaten down|Et dissipati sunt anguli earum]], that is, the chief cities, or the princes of this people, in whose protection the others trusted, and in whom they wished to lie hidden as in corners [*anguli* is "corners", which the Douay-Rheims renders "towers"]. [[3:6|I have made their ways desert|Desertas feci vias eorum]], that is, the ways of that nation just spoken of, [[3:6|so that there is none that passeth by|eo quod non sit qui transeat per eas]] [a note in the edition gives here the Vulgate's reading, *dum non est*]. For roads commonly fail when travellers fail and the lands are laid waste. [[3:6|their cities are desolate|Desolatæ sunt civitates eorum]], namely those of the Jews, [[3:6|there is not a man remaining|non remanente in eis viro]] in them, [[3:6|nor any inhabitant|neque ullo habitatore]] who is a Jew.

paras.t: Dixi, ego Dominus veritas sempiterna, et virtus immensa, cujus dixisse, fecisse est, dum volo : Attamen timebis me : id est, castigationibus istis, quas tibi induxi, non obstantibus, tandem aliquando converteris ad me, et filialem ad me timorem concipies ; suscipies disciplinam, id est, informationem et correctionem paternam æquanimiter feres : quum Salomon scribat : Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam ; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis. Et non peribit habitaculum ejus in toto, quantum ad justos præcipue, propter omnia in quibus visitavi eam, id est propter peccata ob quæ eos afflixi, vel propter mala pœnalia quæ super eos induxi : propter quæ quasi placatus habitaculum aliquod eis concessi, videlicet synagogam sive ecclesiam, vel domus ad immorandum, sive in terra sua, vel aliena. Verumtamen diluculo surgentes, id est mane et cito ad illicita properantes, corruperunt omnes cogitationes suas, pravis cogitationibus adjiciendo consensum. Istud ad alios quam de bonis, de quibus jam dixit, Attamen timebis me, referre oportet, vel ad eosdem secundum temporum intervalla, ut qui ad tempus timuerunt, nec perseveraverunt in bono.
paras.en: [[3:7|I said|Dixi]], I the Lord, the everlasting Truth and the boundless Power, for whom to have said is to have done, whenever I will: [[3:7|Surely thou wilt fear me|Attamen timebis me]]: that is, notwithstanding these chastisements which I have brought upon thee, thou wilt at length one day be converted to me, and conceive a filial fear of me [that is, the fear of a son who dreads to offend his father, as distinct from the servile fear of punishment]; [[3:7|thou wilt receive correction|suscipies disciplinam]], that is, thou wilt bear fatherly instruction and correction with an even mind: since Solomon writes: [[Prov 15:32|He that rejecteth instruction, despiseth his own soul: but he that yieldeth to reproof, possesseth understanding.|Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam ; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis]] [the Latin has *possessor est cordis*, "is master of his heart"]. [[3:7|and her dwelling shall not perish|Et non peribit habitaculum ejus]] altogether, especially as regards the just, [[3:7|for all things wherein I have visited her|propter omnia in quibus visitavi eam]], that is, because of the sins for which I afflicted them, or because of the penal evils which I brought upon them: on account of which, as though appeased, I granted them some dwelling, namely a synagogue or a church, or houses to dwell in, whether in their own land or in a foreign one. [[3:7|but they rose early|Verumtamen diluculo surgentes]], that is, hastening in the morning and quickly to unlawful things, [[3:7|and corrupted all their thoughts|corruperunt omnes cogitationes suas]], adding consent to wicked thoughts. This must be referred to others than the good, of whom he has just said, [[3:7|Surely thou wilt fear me|Attamen timebis me]]; or to the same men at different intervals of time, as those who feared for a time and did not persevere in good.

paras.t: Præterea, hæc est præcipua ratio difficultatis intelligendi Prophetas, quod ea quæ uno passu dicuntur, et satis faciliter intelligi posse videntur, verba mox sequentia impedire cernuntur, sicut et loco præsenti. Nam quum paulo ante jam dixerit, Desolatæ sunt civitates nullo remanente habitatore, mox addidit, Non peribit habitaculum ejus. Rursus quum dixisset, Attamen timebis me, mox subjunxit, Corruperunt omnes cogitationes suas.
paras.en: Moreover, this is the chief reason why the Prophets are hard to understand: that what is said in one passage, and seems easy enough to understand, is seen to be hindered by the words that follow straight after, as in the present place too. For when he had said a little before, [[3:6|their cities are desolate|Desolatæ sunt civitates]], with no inhabitant remaining, he presently added, [[3:7|her dwelling shall not perish|Non peribit habitaculum ejus]]. Again, when he had said, [[3:7|Surely thou wilt fear me|Attamen timebis me]], he presently subjoined, [[3:7|corrupted all their thoughts|Corruperunt omnes cogitationes suas]].

paras.t: Insuper quidam omnia jam in isto capitulo explanata, referunt ad Judæos pro tempore Christi, cujus vocem et disciplinam pro majori parte spreverunt. Quorum principes, videlicet sacerdotes, Scribæ et Pharisæi, fuerunt crudeles in Christum, et quasi lupi rapaces in subditos. Prophetæ quoque Jerusalem fuerunt vesani et pseudo, dicentes : Si dimittimus eum sic, omnes credent in eum ; et venient Romani, et tollent locum nostrum et gentem. Similiter Caiphas : Expedit vobis, inquiens, ut unus moriatur homo pro populo. Sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum : quibus Christus in Evangelio ait, Irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditiones vestras. Sed et Christo Sancto Sanctorum multa crimina imposuerunt. Dominus justus, videlicet Christus, in medio ejus, quia in Jerusalem sæpius prædicavit ; qui etiam mane judicium suum dedit, ipsos Judæos increpando, atque judicium discretionis in eos exercendo : quibus et dixit, Multa habeo judicare de vobis. Porro quod subditur, Disperdidi gentes, exponunt de oppressione Judæorum a Romanis. Deinde illud, Attamen timebis me, intelligunt de credentibus in Dominum Jesum ; id vero, Corruperunt cogitationes suas, de his qui fuerunt increduli. Alii præinducta exponunt pro tempore captivitatem Babylonicam præcedente, et de Judæorum a Babyloniis oppressione tempore Sedeciæ.
paras.en: Besides, some refer everything already explained in this chapter to the Jews at the time of Christ, whose voice and discipline they for the most part despised. Their princes, namely the priests, Scribes and Pharisees, were cruel towards Christ, and like ravening wolves towards their subjects. The prophets of Jerusalem too were senseless and false, saying: [[John 11:48|If we let him alone so, all will believe in him; and the Romans will come, and take away our place and nation|Si dimittimus eum sic, omnes credent in eum ; et venient Romani, et tollent locum nostrum et gentem]]. Likewise Caiphas: [[John 11:50|it is expedient for you|Expedit vobis]], he says, [[John 11:50|that one man should die for the people|ut unus moriatur homo pro populo]]. [[3:4|her priests have polluted the sanctuary|Sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum]]: to whom Christ says in the Gospel, [[Matt 15:6|you have made void the commandment of God for your tradition|Irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditiones vestras]]. And they even laid many crimes upon Christ, the Holy of Holies. [[3:5|The just Lord|Dominus justus]], namely Christ, [[3:5|is in the midst thereof|in medio ejus]], since He preached often in Jerusalem; who also [[3:5|in the morning|mane]] gave [[3:5|his judgment|judicium suum]], rebuking the Jews themselves and exercising the judgment of discernment upon them: to whom He also said, [[John 8:26|Many things I have|Multa habeo]] [[John 8:26|to judge of you|judicare de vobis]]. Further, what follows, [[3:6|I have destroyed the nations|Disperdidi gentes]], they expound of the oppression of the Jews by the Romans. Then that, [[3:7|Surely thou wilt fear me|Attamen timebis me]], they understand of those who believed in the Lord Jesus; but that, [[3:7|corrupted all their thoughts|Corruperunt cogitationes suas]], of those who were unbelieving. Others expound the foregoing of the time before the Babylonian captivity, and of the oppression of the Jews by the Babylonians in the time of Sedecias[[4 Kings 25:8||]].

paras.t: Quapropter exspecta me, dicit Dominus, in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum. Sicut B. Hieronymus refert, Judæi hunc locum exponunt pro tempore Christi, quem putant nondum venisse, quo (ut asserunt) veniente, et mundi monarchiam tenente, gentes et regna ac principes interficientur ab ipso. Hæc autem expositio vana est, quum Christum jam venisse sciamus. Sed diversis expositionibus propter prolixitatem vitandam omissis, locus iste pro tempore Christi præterito exponetur, ut sit sensus :
paras.en: [[3:8|Wherefore expect me, saith the Lord, in the day of my resurrection that is to come|Quapropter exspecta me, dicit Dominus, in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum]]. As blessed Jerome reports, the Jews expound this place of the time of Christ, who they think has not yet come; when He comes (so they assert) and holds the monarchy of the world, nations and kingdoms and princes will be slain by Him. But this exposition is vain, since we know that Christ has already come. Leaving aside, then, the various expositions so as to avoid prolixity, this place will be expounded of the time of Christ, now past, so that the sense is:

paras.t: Quapropter, id est, quia (ut dictum est) quidam Judæorum credent in Christum et jam crediderunt, quidam vero, imo pro maxima parte, in incredulitate manserunt, præsertim usque Apostolorum prædicationem in Jerusalem factam post Christi passionem et Spiritus Sancti missionem, exspecta me tu, popule Judæorum, dicit Dominus Jesus Christus, in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum, id est die qua post mortem tertia die resurgam ; jamque surrexi, sicque exspecta me in futurum, id est perseveranter et semper usque ad mortem et finem ; quia erit judicium meum, id est sapientiæ meæ dictamen, et agendum judicabo, ut congregem gentes et colligam regna spirituali adunatione, convertendo gentiles ad unam fidem et spem, atque individuam caritatem, ut omnes sint unum mysticum corpus Christi in una Ecclesia. Hoc est quod per Isaiam loquitur Dominus : Attendite ad me, populi mei, quia lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in lucem populorum requiescet; et in Psalmo, Adorabunt eum omnes reges, omnes gentes servient ei. Jesus enim moriturus erat pro gente, ut in Joanne legimus. Et ipsemet protestatur Judæis : Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere. Unde et per Isaiam : Gentem, inquit, quam nesciebas, vocabis; et gentes quæ non cognoverunt te, ad te current. Hinc Christus post resurrectionem suam ait Apostolis : Euntes, docete omnes gentes; et, Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ.
paras.en: [[3:8|Wherefore|Quapropter]], that is, because (as has been said) some of the Jews will believe in Christ, and have already believed, while some, indeed the greater part, have remained in unbelief, especially until the preaching of the Apostles made in Jerusalem after the passion of Christ and the sending of the Holy Ghost: [[3:8|expect me|exspecta me]], thou people of the Jews, [[3:8|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]] Jesus Christ, [[3:8|in the day of my resurrection that is to come|in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum]], that is, the day on which I shall rise on the third day after death; and now I have risen; and so expect me in time to come, that is, perseveringly and always, until death and the end; [[3:8|for my judgment|quia erit judicium meum]], that is, the dictate of my wisdom, and I shall judge that it must be done, [[3:8|to assemble the Gentiles, and to gather the kingdoms|ut congregem gentes et colligam regna]] by a spiritual union, converting the gentiles to one faith and hope and to an undivided charity, so that all may be one mystical body of Christ in one Church[[John 17:21||]] [the margin gives John xvii, 21–23]. This is what the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 51:4|Hearken unto me, O my people|Attendite ad me, populi mei]], [[Is 51:4|for a law shall go forth from me, and my judgment shall rest to be a light of the nations|quia lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in lucem populorum requiescet]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 71:11|all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him|Adorabunt eum omnes reges, omnes gentes servient ei]]. For [[John 11:51|Jesus should die for the nation|Jesus enim moriturus erat pro gente]], as we read in John. And He Himself protests to the Jews: [[John 10:16|other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere]]. Hence too through Isaias: [[Is 55:5|thou shalt call a nation|Gentem]], He says, [[Is 55:5|which thou knewest not|quam nesciebas, vocabis]]: and [[Is 55:5|the nations that knew not thee shall run to thee|et gentes quæ non cognoverunt te, ad te current]]. Hence Christ after His resurrection says to the Apostles: [[Matt 28:19|Going therefore, teach ye all nations|Euntes, docete omnes gentes]]; and, [[Mark 16:15|preach the gospel to every creature|Prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]].

paras.t: Et effundam super eos indignationem meam, omnem iram furoris mei. In igne enim zeli mei devorabitur omnis terra. Si istud exponatur in malo, nec superioribus, nec subsequentibus consonare videtur. Nam subditur : Quia tunc reddam populis labium electum, ut invocent omnes nomen Domini, et serviant ei humero uno. Potest itaque uno modo de populo Judæorum intelligi : super quos Christus post passionem suam et resurrectionem, indignationem suam effudit, in manus Romanorum eos tradendo, omnem quoque iram furoris sui, eosdem finaliter derelinquendo, gratiam subtrahendo, et perpetue condemnando : sicut in Isaia protestatur, Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea; itemque in Psalmo, Tu autem, Domine, miserere mei, et resuscita me, et retribuam eis; et denuo, Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos. Propter quod dicit Apostolus ad Thessalonicenses : Pervenit super eos ira Dei usque in finem. Tunc quoque in igne zeli Dei, seu in rigore divinæ justitiæ, devorata est omnis terra Judæorum, infidelibus Judæis consumptis, seu inde sublatis, habitaculisque destructis. Secundo exponi potest de gentibus in incredulitate manentibus : super quos Deus indignationem suam effudit, eos juste relinquendo, omni gratia spoliando, atque æternam miseriam infligendo, imo et multos fidelium persecutores in præsenti sæculo dire plagando, sicut in Sanctorum legendis ostenditur. Tunc demum devorata est omnis terra, id est, omnis homo carnalis divinitus reprobatus. Versiculus iste, In igne zeli mei devorabitur omnis terra, est in Isaia scriptus.
paras.en: [[3:8|and to pour upon them my indignation, all my fierce anger|Et effundam super eos indignationem meam, omnem iram furoris mei]]: [[3:8|for with the fire of my jealousy shall all the earth be devoured|In igne enim zeli mei devorabitur omnis terra]]. If this is expounded in a bad sense, it seems to agree neither with what goes before nor with what follows. For there follows: [[3:9|Because then I will restore to the people a chosen lip, that all may call upon the name of the Lord, and may serve him with one shoulder|Quia tunc reddam populis labium electum, ut invocent omnes nomen Domini, et serviant ei humero uno]]. It can therefore be understood in one way of the people of the Jews: upon whom Christ, after His passion and resurrection, poured out His indignation by delivering them into the hands of the Romans, and also all His fierce anger, by finally forsaking them, withdrawing His grace, and condemning them for ever: as He protests in Isaias, [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation, and have trodden them down in my wrath|Calcavi eos in furore meo, et conculcavi eos in ira mea]]; and likewise in the Psalm, [[Ps 40:11|But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: and I will requite them|Tu autem, Domine, miserere mei, et resuscita me, et retribuam eis]]; and again, [[Ps 68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.|Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos]] [the margin gives only Ps. lxviii, 25, for this last verse; the one before it is Ps 40:11]. Wherefore the Apostle says to the Thessalonians: [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|Pervenit super eos ira Dei usque in finem]]. Then too, in the fire of God's jealousy, that is, in the rigour of the divine justice, all the land of the Jews was devoured, the unbelieving Jews being consumed or carried off from it, and their dwellings destroyed. Secondly, it can be expounded of the gentiles who remain in unbelief: upon whom God poured out His indignation by justly forsaking them, stripping them of all grace and inflicting eternal misery, and even by grievously striking many persecutors of the faithful in this present world, as is shown in the legends of the Saints. Then at last all the earth was devoured, that is, every carnal man rejected by God. This little verse, [[3:8|with the fire of my jealousy shall all the earth be devoured|In igne zeli mei devorabitur omnis terra]], is written in Isaias[[Is 66:16||]] [the margin gives "Cf. Is. lxvi, 16, according to the Septuagint"; the same words stand in this book at Soph 1:18].

paras.t: Porro quod subditur, Quia tunc reddam populis labium electum, etc., referendum videtur ad id quod dictum est, Judicium meum, ut congregem gentes et colligam regna. Si vero referatur ad id quod dictum est, Et effundam super eos indignationem meam; tunc ista conjunctio, Quia, non proprie causam directam, sed concomitantiam quamdam insinuat, sicut in Psalmo quo dicitur : Tibi soli peccavi, ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis. Juxta quem modum ad Romanos dicit Apostolus, quod Judæorum delictum salus est gentibus, et illorum amissio, reconciliatio est mundi. Unde et Paulus et Barnabas incredulis dixerunt Judæis : Quia repulistis verbum Dei, ecce convertimur ad gentes. Ita ergo et hoc loco effusio indignationis et iræ Dei super induratos Judæos, assignatur velut causa illuminationis gentilium, secundum quod subditur :
paras.en: Further, what follows, [[3:9|Because then I will restore to the people a chosen lip|Quia tunc reddam populis labium electum]], etc., seems to be referred to what was said, [[3:8|my judgment|Judicium meum]], [[3:8|to assemble the Gentiles, and to gather the kingdoms|ut congregem gentes et colligam regna]]. But if it is referred to what was said, [[3:8|and to pour upon them my indignation|Et effundam super eos indignationem meam]], then this conjunction, *Because*, does not properly signify a direct cause, but a certain concomitance [that is, that the one thing goes along with the other, not that it brings it about], as in the Psalm where it is said: [[Ps 50:6|To thee only have I sinned|Tibi soli peccavi]], [[Ps 50:6|that thou mayst be justified in thy words|ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis]]. In this way the Apostle says to the Romans that the offence of the Jews is salvation to the Gentiles[[Rom 11:11||]][[Rom 11:12||]], and that [[Rom 11:15|the loss of them be the reconciliation of the world|illorum amissio, reconciliatio est mundi]]. Hence also Paul and Barnabas said to the unbelieving Jews: [[Acts 13:46|because you reject it|Quia repulistis verbum Dei]], [[Acts 13:46|behold we turn to the Gentiles|ecce convertimur ad gentes]]. So in this place too, the pouring out of God's indignation and wrath upon the hardened Jews is assigned as though it were the cause of the enlightenment of the gentiles, according to what follows:

paras.t: Quia tunc, dum gentes congregabo ad fidem, et Judæos destruxero per Romanos, reddam populis labium electum, id est salutarem loquelam atque salubrem confessionem, ita ut omnis lingua confiteatur quia Dominus Jesus in gloria est Dei Patris; ut invocent omnes nomen Domini, id est verum Deum, unum ac trinum. Vel per nomen Domini specialiter intelligendus est hoc loco Dominus Jesus Christus, secundum quod Lyra quadam allegat in glossa Hebræorum super Genesim, taliter dictum : Tunc convertam ad populos labium electum, ad invocandum nomen Domini, et ad colendum eum humero uno. Et subditur : Non est autem dictum hic nomen Domini, nisi rex Messias. Et serviant ei humero uno, id est mente concordi, jugum legis evangelicæ super se intus deferendo et observando, quemadmodum super humerum corporalem onus portatur. Unde a Daniele dictum est : Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei; item in Psalmo, Benedicentur in ipso omnes tribus terræ, omnes gentes magnificabunt eum. Sic namque Christo servire oportet, qui habitare facit unius moris in domo. Propter quod hortatur Apostolus : Unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum.
paras.en: [[3:9|Because then|Quia tunc]], when I shall gather the gentiles to the faith and destroy the Jews by the Romans, [[3:9|I will restore to the people a chosen lip|reddam populis labium electum]], that is, a saving speech and a wholesome confession, so that [[Phil 2:11|every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father|omnis lingua confiteatur quia Dominus Jesus in gloria est Dei Patris]]; [[3:9|that all may call upon the name of the Lord|ut invocent omnes nomen Domini]], that is, the true God, one and three. Or by *the name of the Lord* is to be understood specially in this place the Lord Jesus Christ, according to what Lyra cites from a certain gloss of the Hebrews on Genesis, which says thus: Then I will turn to the peoples a chosen lip, to call upon the name of the Lord, and to worship him with one shoulder [this verse in a rendering from the Hebrew]. And it adds: Now *the name of the Lord* is said here of none other than the King Messias. [[3:9|and may serve him with one shoulder|Et serviant ei humero uno]], that is, with one accord of mind, inwardly bearing upon themselves the yoke of the law of the Gospel[[Matt 11:29||]] and observing it, as a burden is carried upon the bodily shoulder. Hence it was said by Daniel: [[Dan 7:14|all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him|Omnes populi, tribus et linguæ servient ei]]; likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 71:17|in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: all nations shall magnify him|Benedicentur in ipso omnes tribus terræ, omnes gentes magnificabunt eum]]. For it is thus that we must serve Christ, [[Ps 67:7|who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house|qui habitare facit unius moris in domo]]. Wherefore the Apostle exhorts: [[Rom 15:6|with one mind and with one mouth you may glorify God|Unanimes uno ore honorificetis Deum]].

paras.t: Ultra flumina Æthiopiæ, inde supplices mei : id est, non solum in una terra veros habeo adoratores in spiritu et veritate, ferventer humiliterque orantes, sed a remotissimis terris et Æthiopibus, ac ceteris nationibus erunt me invocantes : sicut in Psalmo prædictum est : Venient legati ex Ægypto; Æthiopia præveniet manus ejus Deo; regna terræ, cantate Deo. Nempe in regionibus his prædicaverunt beati Apostoli, sicut apud Isaiam Christus prædixit : Mittam ex eis qui salvi fuerint, ad gentes, in mare, in Africam et Lydiam, in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe, ad eos qui non audierunt de me. Psalmista quoque : Reminiscentur, inquit, et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ, et adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ gentium. Filii dispersorum meorum, id est filii Judæorum, per mundum hinc inde habitantium, ad fidem conversi, deferent munus mihi, id est, spirituales hostias vel alia quælibet dona mihi devote immolabunt. Vel filii dispersorum istorum, sunt spirituales filii Apostolorum, per totum mundum dispersorum, secundum quod Paulus ait ad Corinthios : Per Evangelium in Christo Jesu ego vos genui; et rursus ad Galatas, Filioli (ait) mei, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis. Hoc est quod ab Isaia fuerat prophetatum : Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebit faciem orbis semine.
paras.en: [[3:10|From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, shall my suppliants|Ultra flumina Æthiopiæ, inde supplices mei]]: that is, not only in one land have I [[John 4:23|true adorers|veros habeo adoratores]] [[John 4:23|in spirit and in truth|in spiritu et veritate]], praying fervently and humbly, but from the most remote lands, from the Ethiopians and the other nations, there will be those who call upon me: as was foretold in the Psalm: [[Ps 67:32|Ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God|Venient legati ex Ægypto; Æthiopia præveniet manus ejus Deo]]; [[Ps 67:33|Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth|regna terræ, cantate Deo]]. For in these regions the blessed Apostles preached, as Christ foretold in Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles into the sea, into Africa, and Lydia|Mittam ex eis qui salvi fuerint, ad gentes, in mare, in Africam et Lydiam]], [[Is 66:19|into Italy, and Greece, to the islands afar off, to them that have not heard of me|in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe, ad eos qui non audierunt de me]]. The Psalmist too: [[Ps 21:28|All the ends of the earth shall remember|Reminiscentur]], he says, [[Ps 21:28|and shall be converted to the Lord: And all the kindreds of the Gentiles shall adore in his sight|et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ, et adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ gentium]]. [[3:10|the children of my dispersed people|Filii dispersorum meorum]], that is, the children of the Jews dwelling here and there through the world, converted to the faith, [[3:10|bring me an offering|deferent munus mihi]], that is, will devoutly offer me spiritual sacrifices or any other gifts. Or the children of these dispersed are the spiritual children of the Apostles, who were dispersed through the whole world, according to what Paul says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 4:15|in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you|Per Evangelium in Christo Jesu ego vos genui]]; and again to the Galatians: [[Gal 4:19|My little children|Filioli]], he says, [[Gal 4:19|of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you|quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis]]. This is what had been prophesied by Isaias: [[Is 27:6|Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed|Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebit faciem orbis semine]].

paras.t: In die illa, scilicet in exordio prædicationis evangelicæ, et tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ, non confunderis, o Judæa vel Synagoga, super cunctis adinventionibus tuis, quibus prævaricata es in me : id est, propter tuos excessus non te confundam, nec derelinquam, sed pœnitentiæ gratiam condonabo. Hoc dicitur quoad electos Judæos : de quibus ait Apostolus ad Romanos, Non repulit Deus plebem suam; et ibidem, Reliquiæ per electionem salvæ factæ sunt. Potestque specialiter referri ad Judæos qui morti Christi consenserunt, et postea pœnituerunt : quibus apud Joannem prædixit Salvator, Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum. De quibus per Jeremiam Dominus loquitur : Prævaricata est in me domus Israel, et domus Juda negavit Dominum, et dixerunt : Non est ipse. Quum enim Pilatus dixisset, Ecce rex vester, et, Regem vestrum crucifigam? responderunt, Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem.
paras.en: [[3:11|In that day|In die illa]], namely at the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel and in the time of the primitive Church, [[3:11|thou shalt not be ashamed|non confunderis]], O Judea or Synagogue, [[3:11|for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me|super cunctis adinventionibus tuis, quibus prævaricata es in me]]: that is, for thy excesses I will not confound thee nor forsake thee, but will grant thee the grace of penance. This is said with regard to the elect Jews, of whom the Apostle says to the Romans, [[Rom 11:2|God hath not cast away his people|Non repulit Deus plebem suam]]; and in the same place, [[Rom 11:5|there is a remnant saved according to the election|Reliquiæ per electionem salvæ factæ sunt]]. And it can be referred especially to the Jews who consented to the death of Christ and afterwards repented, to whom the Saviour foretold in John, [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]]. Of them the Lord speaks through Jeremias: [[Jer 5:11|For the house of Israel, and the house of Juda have greatly transgressed against me|Prævaricata est in me domus Israel, et domus Juda]], [[Jer 5:12|They have denied the Lord, and said, It is not he|negavit Dominum, et dixerunt : Non est ipse]]. For when Pilate had said, [[John 19:14|Behold your king|Ecce rex vester]], and, [[John 19:15|shall I crucify your king?|Regem vestrum crucifigam?]] they answered, [[John 19:15|We have no king but Caesar|Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem]].

paras.t: Quidam ea quæ dicta sunt ab illo loco, Exspecta me in die resurrectionis meæ, usque ad verbum istud, In die illa non confunderis, exponunt de resurrectione ventura in fine mundi, et pro tempore Antichristi; quod vero nunc dicitur, In die illa non confunderis, exponunt pro tempore primi adventus Christi, passionis, resurrectionisque ejus. Quod rationabile non apparet, quum sub eodem contextu ac præcedentia jam dicatur, In die illa non confunderis.
paras.en: Some expound what is said from the place [[3:8|expect me|Exspecta me]] [[3:8|in the day of my resurrection|in die resurrectionis meæ]] down to this word, [[3:11|In that day thou shalt not be ashamed|In die illa non confunderis]], of the resurrection to come at the end of the world, and of the time of Antichrist; but what is now said, [[3:11|In that day thou shalt not be ashamed|In die illa non confunderis]], they expound of the time of Christ's first coming, of his passion and resurrection. This does not seem reasonable, since it is in the same context as what went before that it is now said, [[3:11|In that day thou shalt not be ashamed|In die illa non confunderis]].

paras.t: Quia tunc auferam de medio tui magniloquos superbiæ tuæ : id est, sacerdotes, Scribas, Pharisæos, ceterosque impœnitentes Judæos, Christum et ejus discipulos superbissime blasphemantes, auferam a Jerusalem et Judæa per Romanorum exercitum, a quo occisi fuerunt, sicut et Christus ante passionem prædixisse legitur apud Lucam : Circumdabunt te inimici tui undique, eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ. Et non adjicies exaltari, id est te ipsam inaniter elevare, amplius in monte sancto meo. Nam Judæi tunc conversi, de quibus in Actibus apostolicis habetur, devotissime atque humillime coluerunt Deum in monte Sion, et in templo ibidem constructo : erant enim pariter in porticu Salomonis. Multa quoque turba sacerdotum obediebat fidei, ut Lucas commemorat. Denique Judæi impœnitentes post Christi passionem, non diu poterant se jactare in templo, quoniam cito a Romanis fuit destructum.
paras.en: [[3:11|for then I will take away out of the midst of thee thy proud boasters|Quia tunc auferam de medio tui magniloquos superbiæ tuæ]]: that is, the priests, Scribes, Pharisees and the other impenitent Jews, who blasphemed Christ and his disciples most proudly, I will take away from Jerusalem and Judea by the army of the Romans, by whom they were slain, as Christ too is read to have foretold before his passion, in Luke: [[Luke 19:43|thy enemies shall cast a trench about thee and compass thee round and straiten thee on every side|Circumdabunt te inimici tui undique]] [Denis gives this verse in short], [[Luke 19:44|because thou hast not known the time of thy visitation|eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ]]. [[3:11|and thou shalt no more be lifted up|Et non adjicies exaltari]], that is, to raise thyself up vainly any more, [[3:11|because of my holy mountain|in monte sancto meo]]. For the Jews then converted, of whom we read in the Acts of the Apostles, worshipped God most devoutly and most humbly on Mount Sion, and in the temple built there[[Luke 24:53||]]: for they were together [[Acts 5:12|in Solomon's porch|in porticu Salomonis]]. [[Acts 6:7|A great multitude also of the priests obeyed the faith|Multa quoque turba sacerdotum obediebat fidei]], as Luke records. Lastly, the impenitent Jews could not long boast themselves in the temple after Christ's passion, since it was soon destroyed by the Romans.

paras.t: Et derelinquam in medio tui populum pauperem et egenum, videlicet Apostolos, aliosque ex Judaismo conversos, temporalium divitiarum integerrimos contemptores, quibus erant omnia communia, quorum etiam post modicum tempus obstinati Judæi bona rapuerunt. Septuaginta transtulerunt: Relinquam in te populum mansuetum et humilem. Didicerunt enim a Christo, quia mitis est et humilis corde. Et sperabunt in nomine Domini: sicut et Christus ante passionem præcepit apud Joannem, Manete, inquit, in me; et rursus, Confidite, inquit, ego vici mundum. Unde in Actibus Apostolorum orasse leguntur: Da servis tuis cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum. Et Lucas ibidem: Repleti, inquit, Spiritu Sancto, loquebantur verbum Dei cum fiducia. Non itaque in generis nobilitate, sæculari scientia vel eloquentia, divitiis, potentia, vel aliquo humano præsidio, sed in Domino sunt confisi: cujus solo auxilio prævaluerunt, atque ad tam supernaturalem fidem ac arduam legem mundum converterunt. Non enim obliti fuerunt verbi Domini Jesu Christi: Sine me nihil potestis facere.
paras.en: [[3:12|And I will leave in the midst of thee a poor and needy people|Et derelinquam in medio tui populum pauperem et egenum]], namely the Apostles and the others converted from Judaism, most upright despisers of temporal riches, who had all things common[[Acts 4:32||]], and whose goods the obstinate Jews also plundered a little while after[[Heb 10:34||]]. The Septuagint translated: I will leave in thee a meek and humble people. For they had learned of Christ that he is [[Matt 11:29|meek, and humble of heart|mitis est et humilis corde]]. [[3:12|and they shall hope in the name of the Lord|Et sperabunt in nomine Domini]], as Christ too commanded before his passion, in John: [[John 15:4|Abide|Manete]], he says, [[John 15:4|in me|in me]]; and again, [[John 16:33|have confidence|Confidite]], he says, [[John 16:33|I have overcome the world|ego vici mundum]]. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles they are read to have prayed: [[Acts 4:29|grant unto thy servants that with all confidence they may speak thy word|Da servis tuis cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum]]. And Luke in the same place: [[Acts 4:31|they were all filled|Repleti]], he says, [[Acts 4:31|with the Holy Ghost: and they spoke the word of God with confidence|Spiritu Sancto, loquebantur verbum Dei cum fiducia]]. So it was not in nobility of birth, worldly learning or eloquence, riches, power, or any human help, but in the Lord that they trusted[[Ps 10:2||]]: by whose help alone they prevailed, and converted the world to so supernatural a faith and so hard a law. For they had not forgotten the word of the Lord Jesus Christ: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]].

paras.t: Reliquiæ Israel, id est præfati electi Judæi, aliorum respectu perpauci: de quibus et Christus prædixit, Ego scio quos elegerim; non facient iniquitatem, nec loquentur mendacium. Non tamen venialibus caruerunt, quum dicat Joannes: Si dixerimus, quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus. Apostoli vero Spiritu Sancto recepto, in tantum confirmati fuerunt, quod postmodum nunquam mortaliter peccaverunt. Et non invenietur in ore eorum lingua dolosa. Erant quippe sanctissimæ ac innocentissimæ vitæ, secundum illud Actuum: Erant perseverantes in doctrina Apostolorum, et communicatione fractionis panis, et orationibus; sumebantque cibum cum exsultatione et simplicitate cordis, collaudantes Deum, et habentes gratiam ad omnem plebem. Quoniam ipsi pascentur. Utique delicatissime nutriebantur a Spiritu Sancto internis deliciis, spiritualibus alimentis, pane vitæ et intellectus, superdignissimo Sacramento altaris, bonis operibus. Postremo, ut Lucas in Actibus conscribit, Dividebatur singulis, prout cuique opus erat. Et vere dicere poterant: Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit, in loco pascuæ ibi me collocavit; super aquam refectionis educavit me. Et accubabunt in unitate Ecclesiæ. Hinc in Actibus habetur: Omnes qui credebant, erant pariter. Unde et Jeremias locutus est: In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter. Et non erit qui exterreat eos: parati enim erant pati et mori pro Christo. Apostoli quoque ibant gaudentes, quod digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati. Impleverunt equidem quod docuit Christus: Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere. Quanta autem fuerit discipulorum ante Christi resurrectionem, ascensionem, et Spiritus Sancti missionem formidolositas, inconstantia atque fragilitas, quanta vero post Spiritus Sancti infusionem fuerit eorum constantia, imperterritio, sive securitas, delectabile est pensare in libro Actuum Apostolorum.
paras.en: [[3:13|The remnant of Israel|Reliquiæ Israel]], that is, the aforesaid elect Jews, very few in comparison with the others, of whom Christ too foretold, [[John 13:18|I know whom I have chosen|Ego scio quos elegerim]]; [[3:13|shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies|non facient iniquitatem, nec loquentur mendacium]]. Yet they were not without venial sins, since John says: [[1 John 1:8|If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves|Si dixerimus, quia peccatum non habemus, nos ipsos seducimus]]. But the Apostles, once they had received the Holy Ghost, were so confirmed that afterwards they never sinned mortally. [[3:13|nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth|Et non invenietur in ore eorum lingua dolosa]]. For they were of a most holy and most innocent life, according to that of the Acts: [[Acts 2:42|they were persevering in the doctrine of the apostles and in the communication of the breaking of bread and in prayers|Erant perseverantes in doctrina Apostolorum, et communicatione fractionis panis, et orationibus]]; [[Acts 2:46|they took their meat with gladness and simplicity of heart|sumebantque cibum cum exsultatione et simplicitate cordis]], [[Acts 2:47|Praising God and having favour with all the people|collaudantes Deum, et habentes gratiam ad omnem plebem]]. [[3:13|for they shall feed|Quoniam ipsi pascentur]]. Truly they were most delicately nourished by the Holy Ghost with inward delights, with spiritual food, with [[Ecclus 15:3|the bread of life and understanding|pane vitæ et intellectus]], with the most worthy Sacrament of the altar, with good works. Lastly, as Luke writes in the Acts, [[Acts 2:45|divided them to all, according as every one had need|Dividebatur singulis, prout cuique opus erat]]. And they could truly say: [[Ps 22:1|The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing|Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit]], [[Ps 22:2|He hath set me in a place of pasture. He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment|in loco pascuæ ibi me collocavit; super aquam refectionis educavit me]]. [[3:13|and shall lie down|Et accubabunt]] in the unity of the Church. Hence we read in the Acts: [[Acts 2:44|all they that believed were together|Omnes qui credebant, erant pariter]]. Whence Jeremias too spoke: [[Jer 23:6|In those days shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently|In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter]]. [[3:13|and there shall be none to make them afraid|Et non erit qui exterreat eos]]: for they were ready to suffer and to die for Christ[[Acts 21:13||]]. The Apostles too [[Acts 5:41|went|ibant]] [[Acts 5:41|rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus|gaudentes, quod digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati]]. Indeed they fulfilled what Christ taught: [[Matt 10:28|fear ye not them that kill the body, and are not able to kill the soul|Nolite timere eos qui corpus occidunt, animam autem non possunt occidere]]. And how great was the timidity, inconstancy and frailty of the disciples before Christ's resurrection and ascension and the sending of the Holy Ghost, and how great their constancy, fearlessness or assurance after the pouring in of the Holy Ghost, it is a delight to ponder in the book of the Acts of the Apostles.

paras.t: Postremo, totum istud Dominus apud Isaiam prædixit: Sedebit, inquiens, populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta.
paras.en: Lastly, the Lord foretold all this through Isaias: [[Is 32:18|shall sit|Sedebit]], he says, [[Is 32:18|my people|populus meus]] [[Is 32:18|in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]].

paras.t: Præterea, quæ sequuntur, in tantum de Christi Ecclesia sunt intelligenda, ut S. Hieronymus asserat, aliter sentientem, non esse Christianum. Lætare spirituali lætitia in Domino: in quo solo debet esse omnis gloriatio nostra, dicente Apostolo, Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur; filia Sion, id est, Ecclesia militans, in divinorum speculatione consistens, quæ a Deo filia appellaris, propter paternam ejus dilectionem ad te. Sion quippe speculatio dicitur. Jubila, Israel, id est, plebs christiana, quæ vere digna es Israel appellari, id est Deum fide contemplans. Israel namque Deum videns interpretatur. Lætare in mente, et exsulta, signa interioris lætitiæ exterius ostendendo, in omni corde, id est totis præcordiis intimisque medullis, intellectu, voluntate, memoria, filia Jerusalem, id est, Ecclesia in Christi pace per contemplationem divinorum quiescens.
paras.en: Moreover, what follows is to be understood of the Church of Christ, so much so that St Jerome asserts that one who thinks otherwise is no Christian. [[3:14|Give praise|Lætare]] [Denis reads *Lætare*, "rejoice", where the Vulgate has *Lauda*, "give praise"] with spiritual gladness in the Lord, in whom alone all our glorying ought to be, as the Apostle says, [[2 Cor 10:17|he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]; [[3:14|O daughter of Sion|filia Sion]], that is, the Church militant, abiding in the contemplation of divine things, who art called daughter by God because of his fatherly love towards thee. For Sion means watch-tower [*speculatio*, a looking-out, which Denis also takes as contemplation]. [[3:14|shout, O Israel|Jubila, Israel]], that is, Christian people, who art truly worthy to be called Israel, that is, one contemplating God by faith; for Israel is interpreted "seeing God". [[3:14|be glad|Lætare]] in mind, [[3:14|and rejoice|et exsulta]], showing outwardly the signs of inward gladness, [[3:14|with all thy heart|in omni corde]], that is, with all thy heart's core and inmost marrow, with understanding, will and memory, [[3:14|O daughter of Jerusalem|filia Jerusalem]], that is, the Church resting in the peace of Christ through the contemplation of divine things.

paras.t: Denique sancti Prophetæ frequenter nominibus Sion, Israel et Jerusalem, etiam ad litteram populum christianum seu Christi Ecclesiam, præsertim primitivam, designant, quoniam noverant illam re et nomine istis appellationibus dignam. Infideles enim Judæi istis nominibus indigni censentur. Et in Isaia dicitur eis : Audite verbum Domini, principes Sodomorum ; auribus percipite legem Dei nostri, populus Gomorrhæ. Alibi quoque semen et terra Chanaan nuncupantur; imo non filia, sed meretrix atque adultera ab Isaia, Jeremia et Ezechiele dicuntur. Itaque præinductis verbis Ecclesia Christi, præcipue primitiva, imo et quælibet anima christiana (quæ spiritualiter dicitur Sion propter speculationem; Israel, propter Dei visionem; Jerusalem, propter internam pacem), invitatur ad singularem ac maximam in Deo oblectationem, laudem, et gratiarum actionem, propter ineffabilia beneficia sibi a Christo collata, de quibus subjungitur. Quod autem ad Ecclesiam primitivam præcipue, imo et totam Christi Ecclesiam, referenda sint hæc, patet ex eo quod in præcedentibus verbis de ipsa locutus est sermo divinus. — Sed et eadem ad quæ nunc Sophonias hortatur, in Zacharia scribuntur, ubi dicitur : Exsulta satis, filia Sion; jubila, filia Jerusalem, etc. : quæ ad primum Christi adventum esse referenda, sacratissimus evangelista Matthæus testatur.
paras.en: Moreover, the holy Prophets often designate by the names Sion, Israel and Jerusalem, even in the letter, the Christian people or the Church of Christ, especially the primitive Church, since they knew her to be worthy of these titles in deed and in name. For the unbelieving Jews are judged unworthy of these names. And in Isaias it is said to them: [[Is 1:10|Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom, give ear to the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrha|Audite verbum Domini, principes Sodomorum ; auribus percipite legem Dei nostri, populus Gomorrhæ]]. Elsewhere too they are called the seed[[Dan 13:56||]] and the land of Chanaan[[Ezech 16:3||]]; nay, not daughter, but harlot and adulteress they are called by Isaias[[Is 1:21||]], Jeremias[[Jer 2:20||]] and Ezechiel[[Ezech 16:35||]]. And so by the words set out above the Church of Christ, especially the primitive Church, and indeed any Christian soul (which is spiritually called Sion because of contemplation, Israel because of the vision of God, Jerusalem because of inward peace), is invited to a singular and very great delight in God, to praise and to thanksgiving, for the unspeakable benefits bestowed on her by Christ, of which it goes on to speak. And that these things are to be referred chiefly to the primitive Church, and indeed to the whole Church of Christ, is plain from this, that the divine word spoke of her in the words before. And the same things to which Sophonias now exhorts are written in Zacharias, where it is said: [[Zach 9:9|Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion, shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem|Exsulta satis, filia Sion; jubila, filia Jerusalem]], etc.: which the most sacred evangelist Matthew testifies are to be referred to the first coming of Christ[[Matt 21:5||]].

paras.t: Itaque subditur : Abstulit Dominus Jesus Christus, vel Deus Pater, seu tota superbeatissima Trinitas, unus, verus, ac simplicissimus Deus, per ipsum ut mediatorem, judicium tuum, id est judicium condemnationis, de quo ait Salvator : Qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam, et in judicium non veniet, sed transiit a morte ad vitam; et Psalmista, Non intres in judicium cum servo tuo. Ab hoc namque judicio, et a pœna originalis peccati, quantum ad descensum ad inferos, Christus liberavit Ecclesiam, juxta illud Isaiæ : Præcipitabit Dominus mortem in sempiternum, et opprobrium populi sui auferet. Avertit inimicos tuos: quia ab hostibus visibilibus et invisibilibus redemit electos. Propter quod dixit Salvator discipulis : Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri; et iterum, Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Rex Israel. Iste est rex Messias, de quo scriptum est in Ezechiele : Ego Dominus salvabo gregem meum, et servus meus David princeps eorum. Dominus in medio tui. Hoc est quod Christus in Evangelio ait : Ego in medio vestrum sum, sicut qui ministrat; et, Non relinquam vos orphanos; et, Ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi; et, Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum. Non timebis malum ultra, id est malum pœnæ et temporalem afflictionem. Perfectorum enim est in adversis gaudere, et præsentis vitæ persecutiones ac tribulationes quasi animarum medicinam suscipere. Propterea in Jacobo habetur : Omne gaudium existimate, fratres, quum in diversas tentationes incideritis. Et Salomon ait : Justus quasi leo confidens, absque timore erit. Sed et timorem servilem ac inordinatum non admittunt hujusmodi, dicente Joanne : Perfecta caritas foras mittit timorem; et ibidem, Qui timet, non est perfectus in caritate.
paras.en: And so it goes on: [[3:15|The Lord hath taken away|Abstulit Dominus]], Jesus Christ, or God the Father, or the whole most blessed Trinity, one, true and most simple God, through him as mediator, [[3:15|thy judgment|judicium tuum]], that is, the judgment of condemnation, of which the Saviour says: [[John 6:47|He that believeth in me|Qui credit in me]] [[John 5:24|hath life everlasting: and cometh not into judgment, but is passed from death to life|habet vitam æternam, et in judicium non veniet, sed transiit a morte ad vitam]] [Denis joins the opening of John 6:47 to the words of John 5:24]; and the Psalmist, [[Ps 142:2|enter not into judgment with thy servant|Non intres in judicium cum servo tuo]]. For from this judgment, and from the penalty of original sin as regards the descent into hell, Christ set the Church free, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 25:8|He shall cast death down headlong for ever|Præcipitabit Dominus mortem in sempiternum]], [[Is 25:8|and the reproach of his people he shall take away|et opprobrium populi sui auferet]]. [[3:15|he hath turned away thy enemies|Avertit inimicos tuos]]: for he redeemed the elect from their visible and invisible foes. Wherefore the Saviour said to his disciples: [[Luke 21:15|I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to resist and gainsay|Ego dabo vobis os et sapientiam, cui non poterunt resistere et contradicere omnes adversarii vestri]]; and again, [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. [[3:15|the king of Israel|Rex Israel]]. This is the king Messias, of whom it is written in Ezechiel: I the Lord [[Ezech 34:22|will save my flock|salvabo gregem meum]], and [[Ezech 34:24|my servant David the prince|servus meus David princeps]] of them [Denis joins Ezech 34:22 and 34:24]. [[3:15|the Lord, is in the midst of thee|Dominus in medio tui]]. This is what Christ says in the Gospel: [[Luke 22:27|I am in the midst of you, as he that serveth|Ego in medio vestrum sum, sicut qui ministrat]]; and, [[John 14:18|I will not leave you orphans|Non relinquam vos orphanos]]; and, [[Matt 28:20|I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ego vobiscum sum cunctis diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]]; and, [[Matt 18:20|where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them|Ubi fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum]]. [[3:15|thou shalt fear evil no more|Non timebis malum ultra]], that is, the evil of punishment and temporal affliction. For it belongs to the perfect to rejoice in adversity, and to take the persecutions and tribulations of the present life as a medicine for souls. Therefore we read in James: [[Jas 1:2|count it all joy|Omne gaudium existimate]], brethren, [[Jas 1:2|when you shall fall into divers temptations|quum in diversas tentationes incideritis]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 28:1|the just, bold as a lion, shall be without dread|Justus quasi leo confidens, absque timore erit]]. Nor do such men admit servile and inordinate fear [servile fear: fear of punishment rather than love of God], as John says: [[1 John 4:18|perfect charity casteth out fear|Perfecta caritas foras mittit timorem]]; and in the same place, [[1 John 4:18|he that feareth is not perfected in charity|Qui timet, non est perfectus in caritate]].

paras.t: In die illa, tempore primitivæ Ecclesiæ, dicetur Jerusalem, id est congregationi fidelium, quæ in Jerusalem Spiritum Sanctum recepit, et suæ perfectionis initium sumpsit : Noli timere, Sion, carnali et inordinato timore præsentis vitæ adversa, et persequentium tela. Hoc enim docuerunt Apostoli. Unde ait Salvator : Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. In Isaia quoque habetur : Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit? Sit ergo cor nostrum in Deo semper confidens ; atque in ejus pietate sperantes, ejusque dispositioni nos humiliter committentes, parati simus ad omne agendum ac patiendum quod ei placuerit, ut cum justo dicamus : Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea : quem timebo? Dominus protector vitæ meæ : a quo trepidabo? Et rursus, Non timebo millia populi circumdantis me; itemque, Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum. Non dissolvantur manus tuæ, id est, a bono inchoato non cesses neque tepescas.
paras.en: [[3:16|In that day|In die illa]], in the time of the primitive Church, [[3:16|it shall be said to Jerusalem|dicetur Jerusalem]], that is, to the congregation of the faithful which received the Holy Ghost in Jerusalem and took there the beginning of its perfection: [[3:16|Fear not|Noli timere]], [[3:16|Sion|Sion]], with a carnal and inordinate fear, the adversities of the present life and the darts of persecutors. For this the Apostles taught. Whence the Saviour says: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum]]. In Isaias too we read: [[Is 51:12|who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a mortal man, and of the son of man, who shall wither away like grass?|Quis tu ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis, qui quasi fœnum arescit?]] [the margin gives Is. ii, 12; the words are Is 51:12]. Let our heart then be ever trusting in God; and hoping in his goodness and humbly committing ourselves to his disposing, let us be ready to do and to suffer all that shall please him, so that we may say with the just man: [[Ps 26:1|The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life: of whom shall I be afraid?|Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea : quem timebo? Dominus protector vitæ meæ : a quo trepidabo?]] And again, [[Ps 3:7|I will not fear thousands of the people surrounding me|Non timebo millia populi circumdantis me]]; and likewise, [[Ps 56:8|My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready|Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum]]. [[3:16|Let not thy hands be weakened|Non dissolvantur manus tuæ]], that is, do not cease from the good thou hast begun, nor grow lukewarm.

paras.t: Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui fortis. Christus enim Deus et homo, vere fortis atque omnipotens, in medio est suorum, et ipse cum Patre ac Spiritu Sancto ad electorum corda venit, ac ea inhabitat, ita quod templum Dei dicuntur. Propter quod in Apocalypsi habetur: Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis ; et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis, erit eorum Deus. Ipse salvabit vos de morte æterna, imo tandem ab omni pœna atque miseria. Hoc totum in Isaia sic legitur : Confortate manus dissolutas, et nolite timere; ecce Deus vester veniet, et salvabit vos. Hinc demum hortatur Apostolus : Manus dissolutas erigite, et rectos facite gressus pedibus vestris, ut non claudicans quis erret, magis autem salvetur. Hinc quoque secundo libro Paralipomenon legitur : Vos autem confortamini, et non dissolvantur manus vestræ; erit enim merces operi vestro.
paras.en: [[3:17|The Lord thy God in the midst of thee is mighty|Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui fortis]]. For Christ, God and man, truly mighty and almighty, is in the midst of his own; and he himself, with the Father and the Holy Ghost, comes to the hearts of the elect and dwells in them, so that they are called the temple of God. Wherefore we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:3|Behold the tabernacle of God with men: and he will dwell with them. And they shall be his people: and God himself with them shall be their God|Ecce tabernaculum Dei cum hominibus, et habitabit cum eis ; et ipsi populus ejus erunt, et ipse Deus cum eis, erit eorum Deus]]. [[3:17|he will save|Ipse salvabit]] you from eternal death, nay at last from all punishment and misery. All this is read thus in Isaias: [[Is 35:3|Strengthen ye the feeble hands|Confortate manus dissolutas]], [[Is 35:4|and fear not|et nolite timere]]; [[Is 35:4|behold your God|ecce Deus vester]] [[Is 35:4|will come and will save you|veniet, et salvabit vos]]. Hence too the Apostle exhorts: [[Heb 12:12|lift up the hands which hang down|Manus dissolutas erigite]], [[Heb 12:13|make straight steps with your feet: that no one, halting, may go out of the way; but rather be healed|rectos facite gressus pedibus vestris, ut non claudicans quis erret, magis autem salvetur]] [Denis reads *salvetur*, "be saved", where the Vulgate has *sanetur*, "be healed"]. Hence too we read in the second book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 15:7|Do you therefore take courage, and let not your hands be weakened: for there shall be a reward for your work|Vos autem confortamini, et non dissolvantur manus vestræ; erit enim merces operi vestro]].

paras.t: Gaudebit super te in lætitia, id est, de tua stabilitate et gratia ac salute lætabitur in se ipso, lætitia increata, non aliunde causata : quemadmodum scriptum est in Psalmo, Beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo; et, Lætabitur Deus in operibus suis. Hinc in Jeremia fatetur : Lætabor super eis quum eis benefecero. Et Esdras inducit : Gaudium Domini est fortitudo vestra. Silebit super te in dilectione tua, id est, peccata tua tacebit, eo quod diligat te, et propter caritatem qua eum amasti : quoniam caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum. Unde per Isaiam locutus est : Juravi, ut non irascar tibi, et non increpem te. Et exsultabit super te in laude, id est, præconiis quibus eum collaudas, complacentiam piam habebit, et laus tua ei placebit. Vel, Exsultabit super te in laude, ita quod laudabilem te esse testabitur : secundum quod Christus in Evangelio dicit, Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo. Porro in his verbis demonstratur paterna dilectio ineffabilisque benignitas Dei ad nos.
paras.en: [[3:17|he will rejoice over thee with gladness|Gaudebit super te in lætitia]], that is, he will be glad in himself of thy steadfastness, grace and salvation, with an uncreated gladness, caused by nothing outside him: as it is written in the Psalm, [[Ps 149:4|the Lord is well pleased with his people|Beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo]]; and, [[Ps 103:31|the Lord shall rejoice in his works|Lætabitur Deus in operibus suis]]. Hence he declares in Jeremias: [[Jer 32:41|I will rejoice over them, when I shall do them good|Lætabor super eis quum eis benefecero]]. And Esdras brings in: [[2 Esd 8:10|the joy of the Lord is our strength|Gaudium Domini est fortitudo vestra]] [Denis has *vestra*, "your", where the Vulgate has *nostra*, "our"]. [[3:17|he will be silent|Silebit super te]] over thee in thy love [Denis reads *in dilectione tua*, "in thy love", where the Vulgate has *sua*, "his"], that is, he will keep silence about thy sins, because he loves thee, and because of the charity with which thou hast loved him: for [[1 Pet 4:8|charity covereth a multitude of sins|caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum]]. Hence he spoke through Isaias: [[Is 54:9|so have I sworn not to be angry with thee, and not to rebuke thee|Juravi, ut non irascar tibi, et non increpem te]]. [[3:17|he will be joyful over thee in praise|Et exsultabit super te in laude]], that is, in the praises with which thou praisest him he will take a loving pleasure, and thy praise will please him. Or, [[3:17|he will be joyful over thee in praise|Exsultabit super te in laude]], in that he will testify that thou art praiseworthy, according to what Christ says in the Gospel: Every one [[Matt 10:32|that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father|Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo]]. Moreover, in these words the fatherly love and the unspeakable kindness of God towards us is shown.

paras.t: Nugas, id est mendaces et vanos, Christum negantes, qui a lege divina recesserant per inobedientiam et peccata, congregabo collegio fidelium, convertendo eos ad fidem : quemadmodum in Actibus Apostolorum leguntur multa millia Judæorum ad S. Petri prædicationem conversa; quia ex te erant, id est de numero salvandorum seu electorum. Unde et Lucas in Actibus Apostolorum : Crediderunt, inquit, quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam æternam. Et de reprobis in prima sua Canonica ait Joannes : In nobis erant, sed non erant ex nobis; nam si ex nobis fuissent, mansissent utique nobiscum. Ut non ultra habeas super eis opprobrium, de eorum infidelitate et obstinatione erubescendo. Si enim nullus ex Judæis conversus fuisset, potuissent gentiles et infideles Judæi insultare Apostolis primisque credentibus, quod nullus de plebe eorum fidei consensisset.
paras.en: [[3:18|The triflers|Nugas]], that is, liars and vain men, denying Christ, [[3:18|that were departed from the law|qui a lege divina recesserant]] of God by disobedience and sins, [[3:18|I will gather together|congregabo]] into the fellowship of the faithful, converting them to the faith: as we read in the Acts of the Apostles that many thousands of the Jews were converted at the preaching of St Peter; [[3:18|because they were of thee|quia ex te erant]], that is, of the number of those to be saved, or of the elect. Whence Luke too in the Acts of the Apostles: [[Acts 13:48|believed|Crediderunt]], he says, [[Acts 13:48|as many as were ordained to life everlasting|quotquot præordinati erant ad vitam æternam]]. And of the reprobate John says in his first Canonical Epistle: They were among us, [[1 John 2:19|but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us|sed non erant ex nobis; nam si ex nobis fuissent, mansissent utique nobiscum]]. [[3:18|that thou mayest no more suffer reproach for them|Ut non ultra habeas super eis opprobrium]], blushing at their unbelief and obstinacy. For if none of the Jews had been converted, the Gentiles and the unbelieving Jews could have taunted the Apostles and the first believers that none of their own people had consented to the faith.

paras.t: Ecce ego interficiam omnes qui afflixerunt te in tempore illo. Judæos enim incredulos qui primitivam Ecclesiam graviter afflixerunt, Deus omnipotens per manus Romanorum occidit ; et qui corporaliter occisi non fuerunt, spiritualiter perierunt, atque æternam mortem in inferno adepti sunt. Hinc dictum est a Michæa : Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui interibunt. Et salvabo claudicantem, id est virtutibus imperfectam, et fide nutantem, augendo in talibus gratiæ lucem. Christus enim, sicut Isaias prædixit, lucem […] calamum quassatum non contrivit, et linum fumigans non exstinxit. Certum est autem discipulos Christi ante Spiritus Sancti susceptionem sæpius claudicasse.
paras.en: [[3:19|Behold I will cut off all that have afflicted thee at that time|Ecce ego interficiam omnes qui afflixerunt te in tempore illo]]. For the unbelieving Jews who grievously afflicted the primitive Church, almighty God slew by the hands of the Romans; and those who were not slain in body perished in spirit, and gained eternal death in hell. Hence it was said by Micheas: [[Mich 5:9|Thy hand shall be lifted up over thy enemies, and all thy enemies shall be cut off|Exaltabitur manus tua super hostes tuos, et omnes inimici tui interibunt]]. [[3:19|and I will save her that halteth|Et salvabo claudicantem]], that is, her that is imperfect in virtues and wavering in faith, by increasing in such the light of grace. For Christ, as Isaias foretold, the light […] [[Is 42:3|The bruised reed he shall not break|calamum quassatum non contrivit]], [[Is 42:3|and smoking flax he shall not quench|et linum fumigans non exstinxit]] [some words are lost here in the copy of the text; what survives is Is 42:3, which Denis puts in the past: he did not break, did not quench]. Now it is certain that the disciples of Christ, before they received the Holy Ghost, often halted.

paras.t: Et eam quæ ejecta fuerat, congregabo : id est, plebem credentem in Jesum Christum, quam Judæi extra Synagogam esse censebant, ut legitur in Joanne, per caritatem et dona Spiritus Sancti spiritualiter adunabo. Hoc est quod Psalmista prædixit : Pluviam voluntariam segregabis, Deus, hereditati tuæ; et infirmata est, tu vero perfecisti eam. Et ponam eos in laudem et in nomen, id est, gloriosos atque famosos, sive laudabiles faciam eos, in omni terra confusionis eorum, videlicet in tota Judæa, Galilæa, Samaria, regnis et provinciis paganorum : in quibus Apostoli et ceteri Christiani primo valde contempti fuerunt, sed virtute divina tot fecerunt miracula, et tam innumerabiles converterunt ad fidem, quod ubique a credentibus in summo honore, fama et gloria habiti sunt, sicut in Psalmo legitur prophetatum : Constitues eos principes super omnem terram; et, Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham, quoniam dii fortes terræ vehementer elevati sunt. Unde in Isaia de eis habetur : Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas? Et iterum ibidem : Pro eo quod fuisti derelicta et odio habita, ponam te in superbiam sæculorum, gaudium in generationem et generationem.
paras.en: [[3:19|and will gather her that was cast out|Et eam quæ ejecta fuerat, congregabo]]: that is, the people believing in Jesus Christ, whom the Jews held to be outside the Synagogue, as we read in John[[John 9:22||]], I will unite spiritually by charity and the gifts of the Holy Ghost. This is what the Psalmist foretold: [[Ps 67:10|Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect|Pluviam voluntariam segregabis, Deus, hereditati tuæ; et infirmata est, tu vero perfecisti eam]]. [[3:19|and I will get them praise, and a name|Et ponam eos in laudem et in nomen]], that is, I will make them glorious and renowned, or praiseworthy, [[3:19|in all the land where they had been put to confusion|in omni terra confusionis eorum]], namely in all Judea, Galilee, Samaria, and the kingdoms and provinces of the pagans: in which the Apostles and the other Christians were at first greatly despised, but by the divine power they worked so many miracles and converted such countless numbers to the faith that everywhere they were held by believers in the highest honour, fame and glory, as we read prophesied in the Psalm: [[Ps 44:17|thou shalt make them princes over all the earth|Constitues eos principes super omnem terram]]; and, [[Ps 46:10|The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham: for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted|Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham, quoniam dii fortes terræ vehementer elevati sunt]]. Whence in Isaias we read of them: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds, and as doves to their windows?|Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas?]] And again in the same place: [[Is 60:15|Because thou wast forsaken, and hated|Pro eo quod fuisti derelicta et odio habita]], [[Is 60:15|I will make thee to be an everlasting glory, a joy unto generation and generation|ponam te in superbiam sæculorum, gaudium in generationem et generationem]].

paras.t: In tempore illo quo adducam vos, o Apostoli atque credentes, ad aliorum instructionem et conversionem, et in tempore quo congregabo vos, secundum modum nunc dictum; vel, quando congregabo vos gentibus quas convertetis.
paras.en: [[3:20|At that time, when I will bring you|In tempore illo quo adducam vos]], O Apostles and believers, to the instruction and conversion of others, [[3:20|and at the time that I will gather you|et in tempore quo congregabo vos]], in the manner just said; or, when I shall gather you to the Gentiles whom you will convert.

paras.t: Dabo enim vos in nomen et in laudem omnibus populis terræ, quos convertetis, quum convertero captivitatem vestram coram oculis vestris, id est, evidenter eruero vos de adversariorum vestrorum infidelium persecutione et potestate : quod fuit impletum, quando Romani deleverunt Judæos incredulos, et etiam ante ac postea. Frequenter etenim Deus de carceribus et vinculis miraculose redemit fideles, et tyrannos dira morte peremit. Dicit Dominus, qui solus est per essentiam verus ac veritas.
paras.en: [[3:20|for I will give you a name, and praise among all the people of the earth|Dabo enim vos in nomen et in laudem omnibus populis terræ]], whom you will convert, [[3:20|when I shall have brought back your captivity before your eyes|quum convertero captivitatem vestram coram oculis vestris]], that is, I will plainly rescue you from the persecution and power of your unbelieving adversaries: which was fulfilled when the Romans destroyed the unbelieving Jews, and also before and after. For God often delivered the faithful miraculously from prisons and chains, and destroyed tyrants by a dreadful death. [[3:20|saith the Lord|Dicit Dominus]], who alone by essence is true, and truth itself.

paras.t: Præterea, quod in principio hujus capituli de Jerusalem et Synagoga ad litteram expositum est, facile est juxta spiritualem intelligentiam de Ecclesia explanare. Itaque congregationi Christianorum impœnitenti et Christo inobedienti, merito dicitur: Væ provocatrix, et redempta sanguine Christi, civitas, columba propter quosdam innocentes et simplices impiis junctos. Vel, Columba, eo modo quo ait Osee propheta : Ephraim quasi columba seducta, non habens cor. Ista malignantium ecclesia non audit vocem Christi, nec suscipit disciplinam, neque in Deo confidit veraciter, nec Deo appropinquat, se ad gratiam disponendo. Principes ejus quasi leones rugientes : quia cum austeritate atque superbia præsident, subjectosque opprimunt. Judices ejus lupi. Hoc de judicibus injustis et cupidis, munera recipientibus, innocentes inopesque damnantibus, verum est. Prophetæ ejus vesani : id est, prædicantes et docentes populum, allegantes et exponentes Scripturam, et propria verba et documenta non observantes, caput habent insanum, et stultis ac furentibus pares sunt. Sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum, sacramenta irreverenter tractando, et sacerdotales sanctiones transgrediendo. Contra hos dabit Dominus judicium suum mane in luce, id est, velociter, evidenter, atque dirissime eos damnabit. Denique propter Christianorum peccata tradit Deus frequenter terras eorum hostibus suis. Desertas fecit vias eorum, gratiam et virtutes, quibus ad Deum transitur, subtrahendo. Desolatæ sunt civitates eorum : quoniam ipsi damnati sunt, et bonis spiritualibus destituti. Et dixi : Attamen timebis me, suscipies disciplinam. Hoc Dominus ait propter electos. Et non peribit habitaculum tuum : quoniam Ecclesia Christi usque in finem sæculi stabit, ad gloriam Dei sublimis et benedicti. Amen.
paras.en: Moreover, what was expounded at the beginning of this chapter in the letter of Jerusalem and the Synagogue is easily explained of the Church according to the spiritual sense. And so to a congregation of Christians that is impenitent and disobedient to Christ it is deservedly said: [[3:1|Woe to the provoking and redeemed|Væ provocatrix, et redempta]] by the blood of Christ, [[3:1|city, the dove|civitas, columba]], because of certain innocent and simple people joined to the wicked. Or, a dove in the way the prophet Osee says: [[Osee 7:11|Ephraim is become as a dove that is decoyed, not having a heart|Ephraim quasi columba seducta, non habens cor]]. This church of the malignant does not hear the voice of Christ, nor receive discipline, nor truly trust in God, nor draw near to God by disposing herself for grace. [[3:3|Her princes|Principes ejus]] are [[3:3|as roaring lions|quasi leones rugientes]]: for they preside with harshness and pride, and oppress their subjects. [[3:3|her judges|Judices ejus]] are [[3:3|wolves|lupi]]. This is true of judges who are unjust and covetous, take bribes, and condemn the innocent and the poor. [[3:4|Her prophets are senseless|Prophetæ ejus vesani]]: that is, those who preach to and teach the people, who allege and expound the Scripture and do not keep their own words and teachings, have a mad head, and are like fools and madmen. [[3:4|her priests have polluted the sanctuary|Sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum]], by handling the sacraments irreverently and transgressing the priestly ordinances. Against these the Lord [[3:5|will bring his judgment|dabit Dominus judicium suum]] [[3:5|in the morning|mane]] [[3:5|to light|in luce]], that is, he will condemn them swiftly, openly and most dreadfully. Moreover, for the sins of Christians God often delivers their lands to their enemies. He hath [[3:6|made their ways desert|Desertas fecit vias eorum]], by withdrawing the grace and virtues by which one passes over to God. [[3:6|their cities are desolate|Desolatæ sunt civitates eorum]]: since they themselves are condemned and stripped of spiritual goods. [[3:7|I said: Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt receive correction|Et dixi : Attamen timebis me, suscipies disciplinam]]. This the Lord says because of the elect. And thy [[3:7|dwelling shall not perish|non peribit habitaculum]] [Denis reads *habitaculum tuum*, "thy dwelling", where the Vulgate has *ejus*, "her"]: since the Church of Christ shall stand until the end of the world, to the glory of God, sublime and blessed. Amen.
